source: cross-examiner verdicts from the research fleets (one agent per contested claim, both lenses)

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: British American Tobacco p.l.c. held 22.91% of ITC through three vehicles on 31 Dec 2025. The cited ITC shareholding-pattern PDF is headed "Shareholding Pattern as on 31st December, 2025". So the date matches. The ownership window started earlier and is still open. ITC's Report and Accounts 2026 (Note on shareholders holding more than 5%) gives Tobacco Manufacturers (India) Ltd 2,54,14,95,863 shares (20.31%) at 31 Mar 2025, falling to 2,22,84,95,863 shares (17.79%) at 31 Mar 2026. That is the same share count as the Dec-2025 filing, so the 22.91% aggregate dates from BAT's May-2025 partial sale and was unchanged through 31 Mar 2026. No date conflict. The 'from' field of 2025-12-31 is the observation date, not the start of the holding.
verdicts.identityTest:
What the cited SHP shows, verified by curl plus pymupdf: Table III, "(2) Institutions (Foreign) (a) Foreign Direct Investment", 3 holders, 2,86,97,62,693 shares, 22.91% (22.78% on a fully diluted A+B+C2 basis). Named holders: "Tobacco Manufacturers (India) Limited 2,22,84,95,863 17.79"; "Myddleton Investment Company Limited 48,63,11,940 3.88"; "Rothmans International Enterprises Limited 15,49,54,890 1.24". The SHP also lists the three as persons acting in concert with each other.

What the SHP does NOT show: it never names British American Tobacco and never says 'wholly-owned'. The BAT attribution comes from other records:
(a) ITC Report and Accounts 2026 (https://www.itcportal.com/content/dam/itc-corporate/open-pdfs/report-and-accounts/ITC-Report-and-Accounts-2026.pdf): "He is a representative of Tobacco Manufacturers (India) Limited ('TMI'), a subsidiary of British American Tobacco p.l.c. ('BAT')". Related parties are listed as "Subsidiaries of British American Tobacco p.l.c. - of which the Company is an associate". Dividend payments went to TMI (Rs 3197.89 cr) and Myddleton (Rs 697.86 cr).
(b) UK Companies House: Myddleton Investment Company Ltd (00207434, registered at Globe House, 1 Water Street, London, BAT's head office) has a single PSC, Weston Investment Company Ltd, holding 75% or more. Rothmans International Enterprises Ltd (02694154, Globe House) has a single PSC, Rothmans International Ltd, holding 75% or more.
(c) TMI is not an Indian company despite its name. It is an overseas company incorporated in the Isle of Man (reg. 000512C; Companies House FC002714; UK establishment opened 1928).

So BAT control of all three vehicles is established. Exact 100% ('wholly-owned') ownership was not read in a primary document, because BAT's own annual report subsidiary list could not be fetched (bat.com returns 403).
verdicts.baseRate: In this file's own sample, 3 of the 6 companies checked have a foreign strategic or industrial holder with a stake of 1% or more (ITC/BAT, Bharti/Singtel-Pastel, Maruti/Suzuki). That is not discriminating, but it doesn't need to be: the claim asserts a fact, not impropriety, and says so. Foreign industrial legacy stakes of this kind are common in Indian large caps (colonial-era or JV parents: Suzuki, Unilever in HUL, Nestle, Siemens and others).
verdicts.denialFound: None needed and none found. The claim alleges no wrongdoing. BAT and ITC both disclose the stake themselves: ITC in its SHP and annual report, BAT by treating ITC as an associate. The parties were not asked. No contrary reporting found (web-search budget exhausted; checked through primary documents instead).
verdicts.innocentReading: This is the whole reading, not an alternative one. ITC began in 1910 as Imperial Tobacco Company of India, owned by BAT's predecessor. BAT kept a minority associate stake after Indianisation. It holds the stake through legacy UK and Isle of Man holding companies that it controls, and it appoints two non-executive directors to ITC's board (S. Panray and A. Singh, both "Representative of TMI as Investor"). The stake fell from about 25.4% to 22.91% when BAT sold part of it in May 2025. ITC reports "Shareholding of Promoters: Nil", so BAT is classified as a public institutional FDI holder, not a promoter.
verdicts.reason: The edge holds on the primary record. All three percentages, the 22.91% aggregate, the FDI category and the 31.12.2025 date match ITC's own SHP to the share. BAT control of the three vehicles is documented by ITC's audited Report and Accounts 2026 ("TMI, a subsidiary of British American Tobacco p.l.c."; related-party note naming BAT subsidiaries) and by Companies House PSC records. The claim-level text has one false statement. It calls BAT "the single largest named foreign shareholder found in this entire file", but the same file records Suzuki Motor Corp at about 58.65% of Maruti Suzuki (reported tier) and says outright that Suzuki exceeds BAT's 22.91%. Separately, 'wholly-owned' is stronger than any primary document actually read (PSC shows 75% or more; BAT's AR, which would state 100%, returned 403). Neither point breaks the edge s=cap:bat, t=co:itc, pred=own, d=22.91%. Both are wording fixes.
verdicts.corrections:
1) Claim text: remove "the single largest named foreign shareholder found in this entire file". Replace with "the largest foreign holder in the five primary SHPs opened in this file". Suzuki's ~58.65% of Maruti (holders file, reported tier) is larger, and the file's own scope and symmetryCheck say so.
2) Replace "wholly-owned" with "BAT-controlled (subsidiaries of British American Tobacco p.l.c. per ITC Report and Accounts 2026; Companies House PSC ≥75% for Myddleton and Rothmans International Enterprises)". Keep "wholly-owned" only if BAT's annual report subsidiary list is retrieved and shows 100%.
3) Add ITC Report and Accounts 2026 as a second src on the edge, since the SHP alone does not name BAT: https://www.itcportal.com/content/dam/itc-corporate/open-pdfs/report-and-accounts/ITC-Report-and-Accounts-2026.pdf. Quote: "Tobacco Manufacturers (India) Limited ('TMI'), a subsidiary of British American Tobacco p.l.c."
4) Entity cap:bat, alias note: Tobacco Manufacturers (India) Ltd is Isle of Man-incorporated (reg. 000512C; UK FC002714), not an Indian company. Myddleton = Companies House 00207434; Rothmans International Enterprises = 02694154.
5) Optionally add 22.78% (fully diluted, % of A+B+C2) and note the stake was about 25.4% before the May-2025 sale (TMI 20.31% at 31.03.2025). TMI remains at 17.79% at 31.03.2026, so the edge can be marked valid through at least that date.
6) The claim is about a company (BAT p.l.c.), not a family or ethnicity, so the kill rule does not apply.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: Suzuki Motor Corporation held about 58.65% of Maruti Suzuki India at 30-Jun-2026. There is no tenure problem, because SMC has been the promoter since the 1982 JV and Maruti has been its subsidiary since 2002. The date holds. Screener's quarterly table reads "Jun 2026 Promoters + ... 58.65%". The NSE exchange API (corporate-share-holdings-master, symbol MARUTI) independently shows "date":"30-JUN-2026","pr_and_prgrp":"58.65","submissionDate":"17-JUL-2026". The 56.28% figure has a date after all: it is stale. Screener's own yearly table has Promoters at 56.28% for Mar 2020 only (56.21% 2017–19, 56.28% Mar 2020, 56.37% 2021–22, 56.48% 2023, 58.19% 2024, 58.28% 2025, 58.53% Mar 2026, 58.65% Jun 2026). So the 'About' text ("SMC currently holds 56.28% of its equity stake") is boilerplate from about March 2020 that was never updated. It is not a rival current figure.
verdicts.identityTest: Target: Maruti Suzuki India Ltd, ISIN INE585B01010, BSE 532500, NSE MARUTI. The NSE record matches this. Source: Suzuki Motor Corporation, Japan, TYO 7269. Screener names it directly: "The Company became a subsidiary of SMC in 2002 ... SMC currently holds 56.28%". The primary record I opened (NSE summary API) reports only the category "promoter and promoter group" = 58.65%. It does not name SMC. The per-holder XBRL (nsearchives.nseindia.com/.../SHP_1694756_17072026101742_WEB.xml) returned Access Denied to curl and 503 to WebFetch, and the BSE shareholding API was also Access Denied. So the step from "promoter group = SMC alone" rests on the aggregator and the company's well-known history, not on a named line in a primary filing I opened. That is plausible and I have no contrary evidence, but it is not documented.
verdicts.baseRate: Foreign parents holding majority promoter stakes in NIFTY 50 companies are rare: Maruti/SMC 58.65%, HUL/Unilever 61.90%, Nestle India/Nestle 62.76% (screener, Jun 2026). That is about 3 of 50 (≈6%), so the property does pick out a small group. However, "the largest single foreign shareholding" is true only inside this file's 15-company sample. Across the full NIFTY 50, Nestle's 62.76% of Nestle India and Unilever's 61.90% of HUL both exceed SMC's 58.65%. Neither company is covered in holders.json. The claim says "found in this file", which is literally accurate, but it will be misread as index-wide unless the scope is stated.
verdicts.denialFound: none found — not asked. None is needed: this is a disclosed, non-adverse ownership fact that Maruti and SMC state openly (SMC calls Maruti its largest subsidiary). No contra is required at reported tier.
verdicts.innocentReading: Nothing here is concealed and nothing needs explaining. Maruti began in 1982 as a Government of India–Suzuki JV. SMC became the majority owner in 2002, and its stake rose over time through ordinary corporate actions. The largest step, 56.48% to 58.19% in Dec 2023, matches the preferential allotment to SMC in the Suzuki Motor Gujarat buyout. The smaller rises in 2026 fit further SMC purchases or allotments. This is a foreign strategic promoter stake, legally disclosed each quarter under SEBI LODR Reg. 31.
verdicts.reason: The core fact survives. The 58.65% promoter-group holding at 30-Jun-2026 is confirmed by screener and independently by NSE's official shareholding API (filed 17-Jul-2026). SMC is the named promoter. The claim's stated uncertainty is wrong: the 56.28% 'About' figure is not a competing figure of unknown date. It exactly matches screener's own Mar-2020 promoter figure, so it is stale text. The discrepancy is resolved in favour of 58.65%, and the "or 56.28%" alternative should be dropped. The tier stays reported rather than documented because the primary per-holder XBRL naming SMC could not be opened (Access Denied/503). The primary record I did open gives only the "promoter and promoter group" total.
verdicts.corrections: 1) text and d: remove "or 56.28% ... different/unstated date" and "the two aggregator figures were not reconciled". Replace with: "58.65% (promoter and promoter group, 30-Jun-2026, NSE shareholding filing submitted 17-Jul-2026; screener 'About' 56.28% is stale and matches the Mar-2020 figure)." 2) srcs: add ["NSE — corporate shareholding master, MARUTI (pr_and_prgrp 58.65, 30-JUN-2026)", "https://www.nseindia.com/api/corporate-share-holdings-master?index=equities&symbol=MARUTI"]. 3) from: keep 2026-06-30. Optionally add prior-period claims with supersededBy: 58.28% (Dec-2024 to Dec-2025), 58.53% (31-Mar-2026). 4) Scope: change "the largest single foreign shareholding found in this file" to add "(15-company sample; not index-wide — Nestle SA 62.76% of Nestle India and Unilever 61.90% of HUL are larger in the NIFTY 50)". Apply the same fix in the symmetryCheck and strongestCounter text and in the cap:suzuki-motor-corporation publicRole. 5) Remove "discrepancy flagged not resolved" from the entity facts and from the voids entry at holders.json line ~670, since it is now resolved. 6) Tier: keep reported. upgradeIf: the NSE/BSE XBRL or the Maruti Reg. 31 PDF is opened and shows the named line "Suzuki Motor Corporation" with its % → documented.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim as a sentence: 'BlackRock/Vanguard (actor) hold ≥1% named stakes (thing) in NIFTY 50 companies (when: latest quarter)'. The filings' as-of dates were checked: RIL 30.06.2026 ('Shareholding Pattern as on June 30, 2026'), HDFC Bank 30.06.2026, ITC 31.12.2025, Bharti Airtel 31.12.2025, SBI 31.03.2025 ('Quarter ending :March 2025'). All fall inside the period the narrative covers, so the claim does not collapse. The dates are mixed, though, and the SBI filing is about 18 months older than asOf 2026-09-26. The narrative text itself should state the dates. The file's gaps section already admits the SBI and ITC lag.
verdicts.identityTest: Every identity matches. Downloaded 2026-09-26 and text-extracted. HDFC Bank: 'VANGUARD TOTAL INTERNATIONAL STOCK INDEX FUND AABTV0442N … 167330626 … 1.25' and 'VANGUARD EMERGING MARKETS STOCK INDEX FUND, A SERIES OF VANGUARD INTERNATIONAL EQUITY INDEX FUNDS AAATY0918K … 158405284 … 1.19'. That makes 2.44% combined, which matches. Also 'GOVERNMENT OF SINGAPORE AAAJG0594R … 2.17' and 'GOVERNMENT PENSION FUND GLOBAL AACCN1454E … 1.34'. Bharti Airtel: 'GOVERNMENT OF SINGAPORE … 1.22%' and 'GOVERNMENT PENSION FUND GLOBAL … 1.06%'. Neither names BlackRock or Vanguard. RIL: the FPI Category I line (16.52%) has no named sub-holder. ITC: the only named FPIs are 'GQG Partners Emerging Markets Equity Fund … 1.79' and 'Goldman Sachs Trust II - Goldman Sachs GQG Partners International Opportunities Fund … 1.42'. SBI: FPI Cat I is 9.37% with no named holder, and 'LIFE INSURANCE CORPORATION OF INDIA … 9.38'. A search of all five texts for blackrock, ishares, vanguard, fidelity, capital group, europacific, kuwait and abu dhabi finds Vanguard only in HDFC Bank and BlackRock/iShares nowhere. Identity rests on PAN-tagged fund names and NBIM's statutory fund name, not on a name match.
verdicts.baseRate: Same five-filing lens run on the comparison set: BlackRock 0/5, Vanguard 1/5 (HDFC Bank), NBIM/GPFG 2/5, GIC/Govt of Singapore 2/5, Capital Group, Fidelity, KIA and ADIA 0/5 each, and LIC (the domestic control) 4/5. BlackRock is therefore the least visible, not the most. The picture is graded, not uniformly alarming, and the lens does not manufacture the finding. The threshold is the weak point. SEBI's Reg 31 format names holders at ≥1% per registration (per PAN), and BlackRock and Vanguard split their holdings across many separately registered funds. So '0 of 5 named ≥1%' is a weak test of their combined stake. It rules out a single concentrated stake; it does not rule out a larger combined total. Rough scale check: the iShares MSCI India ETF reports net assets of '$6,019,525,338 as of Sep 25, 2026' (ishares.com INDA page). That is tiny next to an Indian listed market worth several trillion dollars. The sample is also not random: it is 5 of 50 constituents, chosen as the largest names.
verdicts.denialFound: None found; not asked. Neither BlackRock nor Vanguard was approached, and no statement from either on the 'own India' narrative is recorded. This matters less than usual: the narrative is rated unsupported, so it accuses no one of anything that needs a response. The absence should still be recorded as 'not asked'.
verdicts.innocentReading: Global index funds (MSCI EM/India, FTSE EM, total-international) must hold large Indian companies roughly in proportion to their index weight. Their stakes are minority, passive and spread across dozens of separately registered funds. Because of that split, each registration sits near or under the 1% naming line. Voting control stays with promoters (RIL, Airtel, ITC via BAT), the government (SBI) and domestic institutions such as LIC. Seen this way, the narrative mistakes AUM rankings and ETF index-tracking for ownership and control.
verdicts.reason: Every factual component checks out against the primary filings. BlackRock/iShares appears in none of the five as a named ≥1% holder. Vanguard appears only in HDFC Bank, through two funds (1.25% + 1.19% = 2.44%). The comparison set gives a graded, non-alarming picture. The one weakness is how much the 'unsupported' verdict leans on a ≥1% per-registration disclosure threshold that is built to miss holdings split across funds. That limits how strong the evidence is. It does not overturn the verdict: combined passive minority stakes do not meet any reading of 'own' or 'control', and the one scale figure checked (INDA about $6.0bn) supports that. The status should stay 'unsupported' (not 'debunked'), because combined BlackRock and Vanguard ownership was not measured. The counts are documented; the verdict is our own inference, so it is analytic.
verdicts.corrections: (1) Add the threshold caveat to the narrative text or strongestCounter: 'named ≥1%' is a per-registration SEBI Reg 31 disclosure line, BlackRock and Vanguard hold through many separately registered funds, and a 0/5 count limits single-vehicle concentration but does not measure combined ownership. The strongestCounter's 'not once' is accurate but reads as more than it proves. (2) Vanguard wording: say 'two separate Vanguard index funds each individually cross 1% in HDFC Bank (Total International Stock Index Fund 1.25%; Emerging Markets Stock Index Fund 1.19%; 2.44% combined, as of 30.06.2026)'. (3) Put the filing as-of dates in the narrative text (RIL and HDFC Jun-2026; ITC and Airtel Dec-2025; SBI Mar-2025) and flag SBI as stale. (4) State that the sample is 5 of 50 constituents and non-random (largest names). (5) Add a combined-scale datapoint to support the counter, e.g. iShares MSCI India ETF net assets US$6.02bn as of 2026-09-25 (https://www.ishares.com/us/products/239659/ishares-msci-india-etf), next to total Indian market capitalisation from an NSE or BSE source. Also add BlackRock and Vanguard 13F or N-PORT India totals to whatWouldChangeThis as the deciding fact. (6) Record 'BlackRock/Vanguard: not asked' as the response line. (7) Keep status 'unsupported'. Do not upgrade to 'debunked' until combined ownership is measured.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim restated: "Rothschild & Co (or any Rothschild-branded entity) holds or controls equity in Indian banks, as of the latest quarter." Evidence windows: the HDFC Bank SHP is as of 30.06.2026, which is current. The SBI SHP is as of 31.03.2025, about 18 months before asOf 2026-09-26, and a newer SBI filing exists but was not opened. The ICICI Bank figures are screener.in aggregates through Jun 2026. The windows overlap the claim's present tense closely enough, but SBI is stale and the narrative should say which date each check comes from. There is no chronology failure.
verdicts.identityTest: Mostly passes, with three defects. (1) The narrative gives the institution as "Rothschild & Co (Euronext: ROTH)". Rothschild & Co went private in 2023; the companion file mandates-ventures.json records it as "Euronext: ROTH, until 2023 delisting", and Wikipedia says the family announced in 2023 it would take the firm private. The current-listing identifier is stale. (2) The Indian entity is not identified in this file. It is identified elsewhere: CIN U65990MH1998PTC116788, SEBI Cat-I merchant banker INM000010668 (rothschildandco.com India page, opened). Reuse cap:rothschild-co / cap:rothschild-co-india. (3) "The Rothschilds" as a popular term also covers Edmond de Rothschild, a separate Swiss group with its own fund range, which sits outside the Rothschild & Co perimeter. Checking only Rothschild & Co leaves that name unexamined. This is immaterial at the ≥1% level, where neither name appears, but the identity scope should be stated.
verdicts.baseRate: Among foreign advisory firms, including the SPEC control Lazard as well as Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, JP Morgan and Citi at group level, the share appearing as a named ≥1% holder in the HDFC Bank or SBI SHP is 0 of 6 or more. Absence is therefore about 100% and does not single out Rothschild in either direction. The lens gives Lazard the same "absence" (mandates-ventures.json says so explicitly), so the result is a fact about advisory firms, not about Rothschild. The finding that actually discriminates lies elsewhere. In the two named-holder bank filings, the controlling holder is the Indian State: President of India 57.43% of SBI (SBI SHP 31.03.2025), with LIC at 9.38% of SBI and 4.77% of HDFC Bank. The largest foreign named holders of HDFC Bank are GIC/Government of Singapore (2.17%), Vanguard (two funds, 2.44% combined) and NBIM/GPFG (1.34%). The denominator is thin: 2 named-holder bank filings out of about 12 listed PSBs and about 21 listed private banks. Publish that denominator.
verdicts.denialFound: None found. Rothschild & Co was not asked, and no response is needed because the narrative accuses no documented act by the firm. The firm's own India page (https://www.rothschildandco.com/en/countries/india/) describes its business as "M&A and Strategic Advisory, Global Markets Solutions including fundraising and strategic capital, and Global Financing Solutions and Restructuring & Liability Management". It mentions no banking licence or bank equity stakes. That is a self-description, not a denial.
verdicts.innocentReading: The boring explanation fits completely. Rothschild & Co India is a Mumbai merchant-banking and advisory subsidiary of about 30 bankers that earns deal fees. Indian banks' equity is held by the State (the President of India controls SBI and the other PSBs), by LIC and domestic mutual funds, and by fragmented foreign portfolio investors led by sovereign and index funds (GIC, NBIM, Vanguard). The surname persists as shorthand because of 19th-century banking history (Ferguson), not because of any current Indian shareholding.
verdicts.reason:
The verdict "unsupported" survives. No source shows any Rothschild entity holding Indian bank equity, and the two primary filings opened show the Indian State (57.43% of SBI) and LIC as controlling or major holders. That is a stronger counter than the one the file gives. The supporting prose, however, contains three factual defects that must be fixed before publication.

(a) Overclaim on threshold. The strongestCounter says "not ≥1%, not at any threshold". Both cited SEBI filings state: "The above format needs to disclose name of all holders holding more than 1% of total number of shares." Absence below 1% therefore cannot be established from these sources.

(b) Wrong source count and misused evidence. It says "5 NIFTY 50 companies' shareholding patterns checked, including three of India's largest listed banks". The five named-holder filings include only two banks, HDFC Bank and SBI. ICICI Bank comes only from screener.in aggregates (FIIs 33.79%, DIIs 42.32% at Jun 2026). Those aggregates name no holder, so they cannot evidence the absence of any named holder.

(c) Stale identifier. "Euronext: ROTH" is given as current, but the firm delisted in 2023.

The advisory characterisation is correct but is unsourced in this file. The narrative is a family-as-actor claim, so it must never become an edge. It stays a narrative, rated unsupported, resting on our analytic reading of documented filings.
verdicts.corrections:
1. In strongestCounter, replace "not ≥1%, not at any threshold" with "not as a named holder above 1% (SEBI Reg 31 SHPs name only >1% holders; sub-1% holdings are not visible in this source)".
2. Replace "in any of the 5 NIFTY 50 companies' shareholding patterns checked, including three of India's largest listed banks by market weight (HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and SBI aggregate data; HDFC Bank and SBI named-holder data)" with "in the 5 primary SHPs opened, of which two are banks (HDFC Bank 30.06.2026; SBI 31.03.2025). ICICI Bank was checked only at aggregate level (screener.in), which names no holders and cannot evidence absence." Apply the same fix to the task-level claim text ("ICICI Bank aggregate" cannot support "named shareholder").
3. Change "Rothschild & Co (Euronext: ROTH)" to "Rothschild & Co SCA (formerly Euronext Paris: ROTH, taken private 2023)", and reference cap:rothschild-co / cap:rothschild-co-india (CIN U65990MH1998PTC116788, SEBI INM000010668) from mandates-ventures.json.
4. Add to narrative srcs: ["Rothschild & Co — Our services in India", "https://www.rothschildandco.com/en/countries/india/"] to support the advisory characterisation.
5. Add to strongestCounter the documented control fact: "SBI SHP 31.03.2025: President of India 57.43% (promoter), LIC 9.38%. The controlling shareholder of India's largest bank is the Indian State."
6. Add a symmetry line: "Same lens on Lazard (the SPEC control) and on Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, JP Morgan and Citi: none is a named >1% holder in either bank SHP. The absence is non-discriminating."
7. Add to gaps: "Edmond de Rothschild (a separate Swiss group, not part of Rothschild & Co) was not checked. SBI's latest SHP (FY26 quarters) was not opened. Only 2 of about 33 listed banks were checked at named-holder level."
8. Keep the claim as a narrative only. Never emit an edge with a family ("the Rothschilds") as the actor (kill if proposed as an edge). Status remains "unsupported".

verdicts.dateTest: As a sentence: SEBI issued a granular FPI beneficial-ownership disclosure circular in August 2023, after Hindenburg's report of 24 January 2023. The order of events holds. The one cited source, TaxGuru (Dev Agarwal, published 23 Sep 2025), says "SEBI rolled out new disclosure norms on 10 August 2023, with phased enforcement beginning 1 November." The entity record (cap:sebi-fpi-disclosure-2023) and the companion file (rules-regulators:c019, from 2023-08-24) date the circular 24 August 2023. So the record has two different dates for the same rule, and the text should use the circular date, 24 Aug 2023. The bigger date problem is that the claim describes the 2023 rule as if it still applies. By this file's asOf date (2026-09-26), SEBI's 209th board meeting (24 Mar 2025) had doubled the size threshold from Rs 25,000 cr to Rs 50,000 cr. That change is recorded in rules-regulators:c020, which supersedes c019. There were also carve-outs for no-identified-promoter companies (Mar 2024) and university funds (Aug 2024). And the Adani matter itself moved on: SC expert committee (May 2023), SC judgment (Jan 2024), SEBI's final Adani orders (Sep 2025). The narrative mentions none of these.
verdicts.identityTest: The list "every named ≥1% holder this file actually found (NBIM, GIC, Vanguard, GQG, Google, BAT)" is incomplete. The file's own claim holders:c014 records Pastel Limited, a Mauritius-incorporated vehicle, holding 7.49% of Bharti Airtel as a foreign promoter-group holder. That is the largest foreign line in that filing, and it is the only ≥1% holder in the sample domiciled in the jurisdiction the round-tripping narrative is about. Pastel is Singtel's disclosed vehicle, so the transparency conclusion survives, but leaving it out of a list headed "every" is wrong. The list also mixes categories. BAT's 22.91% is Foreign Direct Investment, not FPI, and Pastel is promoter-group, so neither tests a claim about "FPI money". In the record's strongestCounter, GQG is described as an "index-fund family"; it is an active emerging-markets manager, and it is also the best-known post-Hindenburg buyer of Adani shares. GIC is said to "publish" its holdings; GIC does not publish a holdings list. It appears in these filings only as the named FPI 'GOVERNMENT OF SINGAPORE'. Named sovereigns are transparent on beneficial ownership, but not because they publish holdings, and sovereign/government Category I FPIs were exempt from the size-based granular disclosure in the first place.
verdicts.baseRate: The test used, "named ≥1% holders are transparent", does not discriminate. In a NIFTY 50 company outside the Adani group, a 1% stake is worth thousands of crores, so almost every such named holder is a sovereign, a large regulated fund family or a strategic corporate. In this sample it was 100%, well past the 80% line. Where the narrative actually applies, the figure is different. Hindenburg's own report (hindenburgresearch.com/adani/) found opaque Mauritius FPIs named at ≥1% in Adani company filings: APMS Investment Fund 2.26%, Albula 2.43%, Cresta 2.30%, LTS 1.54% and Elara India Opportunities 3.91% of Adani Green (June 2019), and Lotus Global 4.51% of Adani Enterprises (Dec 2008). Two NIFTY 50 constituents, Adani Enterprises (co:adani-enterprises) and Adani Ports (co:adani-ports), are in research/raw/indices.json, but neither was among the five filings opened. The sample left out the only index members where this lens could tell anything apart.
verdicts.denialFound: None is recorded in this file, and the narrative carries no contra. Records elsewhere in the repository: the SC-appointed expert committee (reported 6 May 2023) found prima facie no regulatory failure and called SEBI's search for the ultimate owners of 13 Adani-linked FPIs potentially "a journey without a destination" (research/raw/capital/rules-regulators.json, rules-regulators:c023, via LiveLaw https://www.livelaw.in/top-stories/supreme-court-sc-adani-hindenburg-report-expert-committee-securities-and-exchange-board-of-india-sebi-regulatory-failure-229112). SEBI's September 2025 final orders dismissed Hindenburg's related-party allegations (cited in that file as atlas energy:doc-sebi-adani-orders-2025). From memory and not re-fetched in this pass, because the search budget was exhausted: the Adani Group published a 413-page rebuttal on 29 Jan 2023 denying the allegations. The narrative should carry these as contra.
verdicts.innocentReading: Large, long-term foreign holders of mega-cap Indian stocks are sovereign funds, index funds and strategic partners because only entities of that size can reach 1% of a NIFTY 50 company. That says nothing either way about round-tripping, which in the documented allegation sat in concentrated positions in one promoter group's stocks. SEBI's 2023 rule can also be read as general housekeeping on beneficial ownership. By most accounts SEBI's stated rationale was circumvention of minimum public shareholding and Press Note 3 rather than Hindenburg by name, so "triggered by Hindenburg" is a press attribution.
verdicts.reason: The claim's central step is wrong. It says opaque FPI ownership "by definition, doesn't disclose" and so would not show up as a named ≥1% line. In fact the opaque Mauritius FPIs Hindenburg flagged were found precisely as named ≥1% lines in Adani company shareholding patterns. Hindenburg wrote that "shareholding lists in India only specifically name foreign funds (FPIs) if they hold more than 1% of equity" and listed APMS, Albula, Cresta, LTS, Elara and Lotus Global from those tables. What the tables hide is the ultimate beneficial owner, not the fund. So the method is not blind to the pattern. It was pointed at five companies, all outside the Adani group, and skipped the two Adani NIFTY 50 constituents where it would have produced a signal. On top of that, the list headed "every" leaves out Pastel Ltd (Mauritius, 7.49% of Bharti Airtel). The record also contains factual errors: GQG as an "index-fund family", GIC "publishes its holdings", and a 10 Aug vs 24 Aug date conflict. It presents the 2023 thresholds as current even though they were superseded in Mar 2025, and it carries no contra. The honest residue is analytic: named-holder tables show fund names, not beneficial owners, and this sample did not include the companies where the allegation lives.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Rewrite the method caveat: "Named-holder tables do list opaque FPIs at ≥1% (Hindenburg found APMS, Albula, Cresta, LTS, Elara and Lotus Global this way in Adani company filings) but never their ultimate beneficial owners. This file's five-company sample excluded Adani Enterprises and Adani Ports, the two NIFTY 50 constituents where the test would discriminate." Add upgradeIf: open the current ADANIENT/ADANIPORTS shareholding patterns and record every named ≥1% FPI with its domicile. 2) Add Pastel Ltd (Mauritius, Singtel promoter-group vehicle, 7.49% of Bharti Airtel, holders:c014) to the "every named ≥1% holder" list, or narrow the list to "FPI-category holders" and drop BAT (FDI). 3) In strongestCounter, change GQG from "index-fund family" to "active emerging-markets manager (SEC-registered, ASX-listed; the major post-Hindenburg Adani buyer)". Remove the statement that GIC publishes its holdings, and note that sovereign/government Category I FPIs were exempt from the size-based disclosure. 4) Resolve the date: circular dated 24 Aug 2023 (TaxGuru's 10 Aug is a different or secondary date). Downgrade "triggered by Hindenburg" to [reported] press attribution, and add a primary SEBI circular URL. 5) Add the supersession: size threshold raised to Rs 50,000 cr on 24 Mar 2025 (rules-regulators:c020), plus the Mar 2024 and Aug 2024 carve-outs. 6) Add contra: SC expert committee May 2023, SC judgment Jan 2024, SEBI Sep 2025 Adani orders, Adani Group's Jan 2023 rebuttal. 7) Tier: keep narrative status "contested", with the method statement tiered analytic plus innocentReading.

verdicts.dateTest: In the claim's format: Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu India quoted a Re 1 transaction-adviser fee and was chosen as winning bidder by DIPAM (Ministry of Finance) after presentations on 28 Nov 2019. Business Standard reported it on 4 Dec 2019 (datePublished 2019-12-04T01:39+05:30, byline Shine Jacob). The mandate ran from late Nov 2019 until DIPAM called off the BPCL sale on 26 May 2022 (companion edge c003). The dates line up. Using from=2019-11-28 is acceptable as the earliest date, though it is the presentation date, not the award date. BS says 'after which the former was selected the successful bidder'.
verdicts.identityTest: BS names 'Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu India'. DIPAM's EoI (cited in c003) names 'Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu India LLP ("DTTILLP")' as Transaction Advisor, so this is the same entity as node cap:deloitte-india. The awarding body is DIPAM, a department of the Ministry of Finance, so min:ministry-of-finance is correct but coarse. A DIPAM node would be more precise if one exists. SBI Caps is correctly identified as the second-lowest bidder.
verdicts.baseRate: Token Re 1 or near-zero bids are the norm for large Indian PSU disinvestment mandates, not an outlier. The article itself cites three: Citi's near-zero bid on the 2010 Coal India IPO, which all six bankers matched (Rs 1,500 paid in total); JM Financial's Re 1 for ONGC's purchase of HPCL; and Deloitte 'tipped' to have bid the same for CONCOR. The same file records KPMG's Re 1 for IDBI Bank in 2021. The property does not single out Deloitte, and nothing in the claim implies wrongdoing. Symmetry check: the identical reading applies to KPMG, JM Financial and Citi, and the rival bidder SBI Caps is state-owned. Nothing is framed around a family, religion or ethnicity.
verdicts.denialFound: None found. Both parties were asked: 'Both Deloitte and SBI Caps did not respond to emailed queries' (BS, 4 Dec 2019, https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/bpcl-sake-sale-deloitte-quotes-just-re-1-as-its-disinvestment-advisory-fee-119120400063_1.html). I found no later correction or contrary report. A new web search was not possible because the search budget was exhausted, so contrary reporting was not searched beyond the repo and the article itself.
verdicts.innocentReading: A loss-leader bid for prestige: a near-zero fee buys a place on India's largest strategic sale. BS carries this explanation twice. An unnamed source says 'For Deloitte, this may be a prestigious deal and will add to its portfolio a national energy company'. Partha Bhattacharya, Coal India chairman at the time of its IPO, says bankers 'don't look at the cash money... could have gone for a notional token figure to get their name associated with this'. Under L1 (lowest-bidder) selection, a Re 1 bid wins on price.
verdicts.reason: The source was fetched with curl after WebFetch returned 403, and it says what the claim says. Quotes: 'Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu India has quoted Rs 1 to manage the sale of Bharat Petroleum Corporation'; 'According to three persons in the know, SBI Caps was the second-lowest bidder with a quote in the range of Rs 15-17 crore. Both Deloitte and SBI Caps did not respond to emailed queries'; 'On November 28, both Deloitte and SBI Caps had made presentations before the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management, after which the former was selected the successful bidder.' The award itself is documented separately by DIPAM's EoI (c003). The fee rests on one credible outlet with a named reporter and anonymous sources, and has no primary confirmation, so 'reported' is the ceiling. The content survives both lenses. The edge encoding does not, and needs the fixes listed in corrections.
verdicts.corrections: (1) Direction: the contract fixes 'award' as awarder→winner. c004 has s=cap:deloitte-india and t=min:ministry-of-finance, which is reversed, and the note 'Direction recorded as fee-quote from adviser to awarder' is not permitted under the contract. Swap the fields to s=min:ministry-of-finance (or a DIPAM node), t=cap:deloitte-india. Better still, drop c004 as a separate edge and put the fee on c003 as an attribute or sub-claim (fee Re 1, tier reported, source BS 4 Dec 2019). c003 already records the same mandate between the same pair, so as things stand the graph shows two award edges for one mandate, one of them backwards. (2) Sourcing wording: the text says 'three anonymous sources' as if they back the Re 1 figure. In the article, the 'three persons in the know' back only the SBI Caps Rs 15–17 crore figure. The Re 1 fee is stated in BS's own voice with no attribution. Suggested text: 'BS reported Deloitte quoted Re 1; SBI Caps second-lowest at Rs 15–17 crore per three unnamed persons; Deloitte and SBI Caps did not respond to emailed queries.' (3) Amount: a=0 misstates Re 1. Use a=0.00000001 (₹ crore), or null with the fee in d, and set benefit.amountCr to match. (4) Dates: keep from=2019-11-28 but label it as the presentation date; selection followed it and came before 4 Dec 2019. to=null is fine for a one-off fee quote, and for the mandate itself use c003's 2022-05-26. (5) Add the Coal India, HPCL/JM Financial, IDBI/KPMG and CONCOR precedents to the record, citing the article, so readers can see that Re 1 bids are routine.

verdicts.baseRate: Being a Big Four firm named DIPAM TA is not a distinguishing fact. Re 1 or token fee bids were common in the 2019-2021 DIPAM tenders: Deloitte bid Re 1 on BPCL (per BS), and KPMG won IDBI Bank at Re 1 (per BS, Aug 2021). The Re 1 detail says nothing specific about Deloitte. It reflects L1 lowest-bid tendering, where advisers buy league-table credit. Symmetry: the same edge shape (ministry awards TA to a firm) applies to every DIPAM adviser across governments, and the record carries no pejorative framing. No family, religion or ethnicity framing.
verdicts.denialFound: None found. Deloitte was not asked, as far as the record shows. verdicts.innocentReading: This is a routine competitive DIPAM tender. The appointment is a disclosed, public government procurement result, not a favour. The CONCOR sale later stalled over the railway land-lease policy, so the mandate may never have produced a success fee.
verdicts.reason: I opened the primary record. The BSE attachment (historical path) is CONCOR's 10.12.2019 letter to BSE/NSE. It names Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu India as Transaction Advisor, L&L Partners as Legal Advisor and RBSA Valuation Advisors LLP as Asset Valuer, appointed by DIPAM letters dated 06.12.2019. The one weak clause is "Deloitte 'tipped' to have bid Re 1 again". It rests on a single unsourced sentence in BS (4 Dec 2019): "Deloitte is tipped to have quoted a similar amount for Container Corporation of India (Concor) as well." That sentence is also cited only in the record, not in the claim's srcs. It is speculation that predates the award and is never confirmed. It must stay a labelled reported/unconfirmed note in 'd' and must not raise the edge's amount or benefit.

Add the source ["CONCOR letter to BSE/NSE, 10.12.2019 — appointment of LA/TA/valuer (DIPAM letters 3/18/2019DIPAM-V dated 06.12.2019)", "https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachHis/9c4972e4-82e6-447d-8d62-0d88c6633234.pdf"]. The AttachLive URL in upgradeIf now returns 404; AttachHis returns the PDF. 2) from: "2019-12" -> "2019-12-06" (date of the DIPAM appointment letters). 3) Claim text: split or mark the Re 1 clause. verdicts.dateTest: Claim: DIPAM (MoF) appointed RBSA as TA for the SCI strategic sale, Dec 2019. The BS article's datePublished is 2019-12-07T19:35 IST. The primary record agrees and narrows the dates. The SCI Preliminary Information Memorandum (DIPAM, 22 Dec 2020, hosted at shipmin.gov.in) says RBSA was appointed "pursuant to a Request for Proposals (RFP) dated 11th October 2019 and subsequent engagement letter dated 8th January 2020". Cabinet gave in-principle approval on 20 Nov 2019. The sequence is RFP (Oct 2019), cabinet approval (Nov 2019), selection reported (7 Dec 2019), engagement letter (8 Jan 2020), PIM/EoI (Dec 2020). There is no anachronism. `from: 2019-12-07` is the date of the report, not a record date. The formal award is the engagement letter of 2020-01-08.
verdicts.identityTest: The entity is only partly right. BS names "RBSA Advisors". The PIM names the contracting entity as "RBSA Capital Advisors LLP, 2nd Floor, IAPL House, 23 South Patel Nagar, New Delhi-110008". The node cap:rbsa-advisors has the label "RBSA Advisors / RBSA Valuation Advisors LLP", which merges it with the separate LLP that was CONCOR's asset valuer (c007). "RBSA Capital Advisors LLP" is only an alias. These are distinct LLPs in the same group. The SCI mandate belongs to RBSA Capital Advisors LLP. The counterparty is correct: the Government of India acting through DIPAM, Ministry of Finance. The NSE ticker SCI matches Shipping Corporation of India Ltd, and the 63.75% stake matches both sources. No LLPIN is recorded; it should be added from the MCA record.
verdicts.baseRate: The file's own base-rate row counts 5 of 7 DIPAM TA mandates in 2019–21 going to Big Four firms. So a non-Big-Four winner is the minority (about 29%), but it is not rare: SBI Caps also won Pawan Hans and is reported for BEML/NINL, and Resurgent India won Central Electronics. An award to a domestic advisory firm does not discriminate on its own. Under the SPEC control, the same "award" edge with "amount not stated" is recorded for Deloitte (BPCL, CONCOR), KPMG (IDBI) and EY (Air India), so the edge is treated symmetrically. The benefit field's gloss, "a domestic mid-size firm beating Big Four rivals on a listed CPSE sale", is not supported. Neither source names the other bidders for the SCI TA RFP, so the claim that it beat Big Four firms is unsourced.
verdicts.denialFound: None found; not asked. None is needed, because the claim alleges no wrongdoing and the appointment is stated in the government's own PIM. The fee is not in either source. The BS article is paywalled after the first paragraph, and the PIM does not disclose the TA fee.
verdicts.innocentReading: This is a routine competitive procurement. DIPAM issued a TA RFP on 11 Oct 2019, selected RBSA (reportedly its second disinvestment mandate), and issued an engagement letter on 8 Jan 2020. RBSA then produced the PIM in Dec 2020. The sale later stalled, like several other CPSE strategic sales. Nothing here implies favour.
verdicts.reason: I could not refute it. The government has a 63.75 per cent equity stake..." (published 7 Dec 2019). verdicts.dateTest: Claim as a sentence: DIPAM (Ministry of Finance) awarded the IDBI Bank strategic-disinvestment transaction-adviser mandate to KPMG India for Re 1, reported 26 Aug 2021. The process window fits. BS of 8 Aug 2021 (datePublished 2021-08-08T14:20+05:30) says the RFP was issued in June and bids closed 13 July, extended to 22 July. It also says the seven firms "would make a virtual presentation before the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management ... on August 10, according to a notice by DIPAM". BS of 26 Aug 2021 (datePublished 2021-08-26T13:02+05:30) reports the selection. The order is RFP, then bids, then presentations, then selection, which is consistent. Two caveats. First, the record's d-field says the firms "presented on 10 Aug 2021", but the source only says they were scheduled to present. Second, KPMG's own reply in the same article says "DIPAM is running the process for selecting a transaction advisor", so the formal appointment may not have been issued by 26 Aug. 'from: 2021-08-26' is therefore the report date, not a documented appointment date.
verdicts.identityTest: BS names the winner as "KPMG India" ("KPMG India has been appointed as the transaction adviser for strategic divestment of IDBI Bank"). It gives no legal entity or CIN, so the operating company could be, for example, KPMG Advisory Services Pvt Ltd; this cannot be determined from the source. The node cap:kpmg-india matches the source's wording. The awarder is DIPAM, which is a department of the Ministry of Finance, so min:ministry-of-finance is acceptable because the file has no DIPAM node. The six rivals match the source exactly: Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu India LLP, Ernst and Young LLP, ICICI Securities, JM Financial Ltd, RBSA Capital Advisors LLP and SBI Capital Markets. Stake figures match: GoI 45.48% and LIC 49.24%. The amount is Re 1; a:0 in crore is an acceptable rounding and matches the BPCL convention in the same file.
verdicts.baseRate: Re 1 or near-zero winning bids are routine in DIPAM transaction-adviser RFPs because selection is L1 (lowest fee) after the technical round. The same BS article says "Deloitte had recently bid Re 1 to manage the privatisation of Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL), and was appointed". The file's own sources add Deloitte on CONCOR (tipped at a similar amount), JM Financial on ONGC–HPCL and Citi on the 2010 Coal India IPO. The property is therefore non-discriminating across Big Four firms and investment banks, and across UPA-era (Coal India 2010) and NDA-era sales. The symmetry control passes: the same lens gives the same reading for the UPA-era deal. The claim alleges no wrongdoing, so the base rate does not refute it; it only rules out any inference that the Re 1 bid singles KPMG out.
verdicts.denialFound: No denial. KPMG was asked. BS writes that the firm said "in response to Business Standard's queries": "With regards to the IDBI bank sale, DIPAM is running the process for selecting a transaction advisor. Hence we would refrain from commenting on the ongoing process." (https://www.business-standard.com/article/economy-policy/kpmg-to-assist-government-in-strategic-divestment-of-idbi-bank-for-rs-1-121082600542_1.html). This is a refusal to comment, not a denial or a confirmation. I found no DIPAM statement: the web search budget was used up, and direct attempts to reach DIPAM, PIB and search-engine pages returned nothing relevant.
verdicts.innocentReading: Under DIPAM's lowest-fee selection rule, advisers bid near zero to win credentials for a flagship bank privatisation. BS itself frames it this way: "Firms have been placing near-zero bids ... as a means to improve their portfolios and establish credentials". KPMG won because it was L1. Nothing in the record suggests favouritism, and the claim implies none.
verdicts.reason: Both BS URLs open (HTTP 200) and support every element of the claim almost word for word. The key sentences are "KPMG India has been appointed as the transaction adviser for strategic divestment of IDBI Bank, and the firm will assist the government in the sale for Re 1" (in BS's own voice) and "KPMG placed the lowest bid of Re 1, and was selected as the transaction adviser, said an official". The seven bidders and KPMG's no-comment are quoted exactly. I found no contrary reporting, though searching was limited. The tier stays at reported: this is one credible outlet stating the appointment in its own voice, backed by an unnamed official, with the party asked and not denying. It is not documented, because no DIPAM order, PIB release or Parliament answer was retrieved and there is no second independent outlet. The CONTRACT's 'reported' requirement asks for named sourcing, and the official here is unnamed. The outlet's own declarative sentence and the transparent 'BS quoting an official' label keep the claim at reported, consistent with the BPCL sibling claim in the same file. I recommend no upgrade until the DIPAM record, such as the Oct 2022 IDBI EoI naming the adviser, is retrieved.
verdicts.corrections: 1) d-field: change "presented on 10 Aug 2021" to "were scheduled to present to DIPAM on 10 Aug 2021 (DIPAM notice cited by BS, 8 Aug 2021)". 2) d-field and text: expand "KPMG declined to comment" to quote that KPMG said "DIPAM is running the process for selecting a transaction advisor", so readers can see formal appointment may not have been issued on 26 Aug. The source says only that KPMG was L1 and was selected; rivals' fees and technical qualification are not published. Rewrite as "KPMG L1 at Re 1; rivals' bids not published". 5) Optional: note in 'sub' or 'd' that the legal entity is unspecified in the source ("KPMG India"; no CIN). 6) Keep upgradeIf as is; add "DIPAM IDBI Bank EoI (Oct 2022) naming the transaction adviser" as a concrete upgrade target.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: DIPAM (Ministry of Finance) awarded Deloitte and SBI Caps the job of pre-IPO transaction adviser for LIC, with the award dated Sep 2020. The only source cited is Bloomberg, run in BS on 22 Aug 2020, 12:04 PM IST. It is a forward-looking story: "India is poised to hire Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu India Ltd. and SBI Capital Markets Ltd. to help Life Insurance Corp. of India prepare for an initial share sale, people with knowledge of the matter said." It traces back to a tender document issued in June 2020. The completed appointment is confirmed by BS's own staff reporters (Shrimi Choudhary and Arup Roychoudhury, 15 Sep 2020): "The Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (Dipam) has appointed pre-IPO transaction advisors — SBI Caps and Deloitte — for LIC's IPO." A BS article from 15 Jul 2021 says the same: "Deloitte and SBI Caps have been appointed as pre-IPO transaction advisors." So the start date from=2020-09 holds, and DIPAM awarding the mandate falls within its own remit. The end date to=2022-05, the LIC listing, has no source and is an inference.
verdicts.identityTest: The awarder is DIPAM, which is a department of the Ministry of Finance. Mapping it to min:ministry-of-finance with the alias DIPAM is acceptable. On the adviser, Bloomberg names "Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu India Ltd.", but the node is labelled "Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu India LLP". The Indian member firm is an LLP, so Bloomberg's "Ltd." suffix is probably loose wording and not a different entity. No LLPIN is recorded on the node, so this has not been checked against the MCA register. SBI Capital Markets Ltd is correct.
verdicts.baseRate: This fact does not single anyone out. DIPAM routinely appoints Big Four firms and SBI Caps, which is state-owned, as transaction advisers: Deloitte for BPCL and CONCOR, SBI Caps for Pawan Hans. Nearly every CPSE disinvestment has one or two such advisers, and adviser fees are almost never published. The advisers control group in SPEC (Rothschild, Lazard, GS, MS, JPM, Citi, Kotak, Axis, Avendus) gets the same fields, and all of them show fee undisclosed as the normal case. The edge implies no wrongdoing, and none should be read into it.
verdicts.denialFound: None found, and nobody appears to have been asked. There is nothing to deny: DIPAM and the advisers did not contest the appointment, and later reporting treated it as established fact.
verdicts.innocentReading: This is a normal procurement. DIPAM issued a tender in June 2020, picked a Big Four firm and the state-owned merchant bank, and gave them LIC's capital structure and restatement of accounts to work on before the IPO. That is routine disinvestment practice and matches the tender described in the source.
verdicts.reason: The claim holds and I could not refute it. The cited Bloomberg/BS article does say the government would hire Deloitte and SBI Capital Markets for LIC pre-IPO work, and that no fee was stated. Two later BS reports confirm the appointment was completed: one by BS staff reporters on 15 Sep 2020, and one on 15 Jul 2021. There are two problems. First, the claim text overstates the source it cites: that source says "poised to hire" and relies on unnamed people, while the confirmation of the actual appointment sits in sources the record does not cite. Symmetry check under SPEC: an Avendus or Axis Capital mandate would be coded client → adviser, with the client being the issuer. The same rule makes Cropnosys the awarder here, not Kotak.
verdicts.denialFound: Nothing to deny, and none found. Neither Rothschild nor Kotak was asked. The Cropnosys/KAAML release (IssueWire) does not name any adviser.
verdicts.innocentReading: Cropnosys, a Bengaluru agrochemical company with Rs 672 crore FY23 revenue, hired Rothschild & Co as its placement adviser to raise growth capital for expanding its Vapi plant. Kotak's special-situations AIF was the investor that bought in. This is an ordinary mid-market advisory mandate. Kotak Mahindra Bank did not award Rothschild anything.

The underlying fact, that Rothschild advised Cropnosys's Rs 375 crore raise in Dec 2023, survives at "reported" (one credible outlet, adviser role described but not named as a formal mandate) as a re-pointed edge.

The same Dealogic count cited in the article puts Morgan Stanley (179) and Citi (165) ahead of Rothschild (151). Having an India league-table rank is a property shared by 100% of the control set, so it does not discriminate. This record gives no symmetric mandate fields for the controls.

The underlying facts check out: the US$360m deal, the rank of #3 by count with 151 deals, the 2023 date, and Rothschild as the CleanMax-side banker. They come from one credible outlet with named on-record sources (Rothschild's co-head India and CleanMax's founder), and Dealogic is named as the data vendor. verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: LSEG Deals Intelligence ranked India advisers for 1H 2024 (1 Jan to 30 Jun 2024), and Rothschild & Co, Lazard and JP Morgan do not appear in the top 10 for fees, announced any-India M&A or India-domiciled ECM. It says nothing about FY2024 or later. The 9M 2024 reporting (India Dispatch, citing LSEG) still has Citi leading M&A and Kotak leading fees, which fits.
verdicts.identityTest: These are league-table entities. LSEG ranks at the brand or parent level, e.g. "Citi", "Kotak Mahindra Bank Ltd", "Goldman Sachs & Co". The target node is cap:rothschild-co-india, the Indian subsidiary. The source shows only that Rothschild & Co, whichever entity, is absent from the ranking. It does not name the subsidiary, and a parent-level absence covers it anyway. The claim is correct in substance, but the edge would identify the entity better if it pointed to the Rothschild & Co group node (or the note said the ranking is group-level). None of the named entities is a family: "Rothschild" here is Rothschild & Co, the institution, as SPEC requires.
verdicts.baseRate: Being absent from a top 10 is the default. The any-India M&A table covers 1,262 deals and hundreds of advisers, so absence alone tells you almost nothing. Measured against the SPEC adviser control set (Rothschild, Lazard, Goldman, Morgan Stanley, JP Morgan, Citi, Kotak, Axis, Avendus), 3 of 9 (33%) are absent from all three tables. That is below the 80% non-discriminating line, so as a comparison within the control set the observation carries some information. The symmetry control is applied, because Lazard and JP Morgan are absent in exactly the same way. The claim does not single out Rothschild.
verdicts.denialFound: None found. Not asked. None is needed: the claim is an analytic observation from a public league table and alleges no wrongdoing.
verdicts.innocentReading: Half-year league tables follow the few largest deals. Citi's M&A number 1 comes from only 5 deals worth $7.5bn, and HSBC and Raine rank 4th on a single $3.1bn deal. Boutique mid-market advisers such as Rothschild and Lazard rarely reach the value-ranked top 10 in a six-month window. Rank-value tables also leave out undisclosed-value and government advisory mandates. The absence says nothing about a franchise's size, health or conduct. The record already carries this reading.
verdicts.reason: I extracted the source PDF with PyMuPDF and every element checks out. The PDF says "Kotak Mahindra Bank took the top position for overall investment banking fee ranking in India with a total of US$40.6 million", and the highlights page lists "M&A TOP FINANCIAL ADVISOR YTD ... Citi" and "ECM TOP BOOK RUNNER YTD ... Citi". Rothschild, Lazard and JP Morgan appear nowhere in them, and none of the three is in the DCM table either. The totals $530.4m and $90.8m also match. The claim is our own comparison, it carries an innocentReading, it applies the symmetry control, and it implies no wrongdoing. Analytic is the right tier. I could not refute it.
verdicts.corrections: (1) Say in the text or `d` that the source has four league tables (fees, any-India M&A, ECM and DCM), and that the three named firms are absent from DCM as well. As written, "all three" suggests the report has only three tables. (2) Point `t` at the Rothschild & Co group node, or add to `d` "LSEG ranks at group level; subsidiary not separately named". verdicts.dateTest: Claim: BlackRock agreed to sell its 40% of DSP BlackRock Investment Managers to DSP Group on 7 May 2018. The deal was announced on 7 May 2018. The cited Reuters/BS piece says "BlackRock Inc on Monday agreed to sell its 40 percent interest in DSP BlackRock". Completion came later: BlackRock's Q3-2018 10-Q and its FY2018 10-K say "In August 2018, the Company completed the sale of its minority interest in DSP BlackRock Investment Managers Pvt. Ltd. to The DSP Group". BlackRock's ownership window was roughly 2006 to August 2018. It inherited Merrill Lynch Investment Managers' 40% of DSP Merrill Lynch in 2006, and the JV was renamed DSP BlackRock in 2008. The edge as encoded has from=2018-05-07 and to=null. For an `own` edge, that says BlackRock's ownership began in May 2018 and is still running, which is the opposite of what happened. The date test fails on the encoding, not on the fact.
verdicts.identityTest: The source names the target as "DSP BlackRock", a JV between "the DSP Group" and BlackRock. The 10-K names it "DSP BlackRock Investment Managers Pvt. Ltd.", with the buyer as "The DSP Group". The edge sets pred=own, s=cap:blackrock, t=cap:dsp-group. Under CONTRACT, `own` runs owner→owned, so this edge says BlackRock owns DSP Group. BlackRock never owned DSP Group; it owned 40% of the AMC. The node cap:dsp-group also merges the buyer (DSP Group, Kothari-led) with the company being sold (DSP BlackRock Investment Managers, later DSP Investment Managers) through its aliases. The subject is identified correctly. The object is conflated and the direction is wrong. No CIN was recorded for the AMC.
verdicts.baseRate: This is not discriminating. Foreign partners leaving Indian AMC JVs, or selling to their Indian partner, was the common pattern of 2012–2019. Examples: Fidelity sold to L&T (2012), Morgan Stanley to HDFC (2013), Daiwa's stake was sold, Goldman Sachs AMC went to Reliance (2015), Deutsche AMC went to DHFL Pramerica (2015), and Nomura sold its LIC Nomura stake. Minority foreign partners exiting is the ordinary outcome, not a signal. The symmetry control (Vanguard, NBIM, GIC, Capital Group, Fidelity, LIC) reads the same way: Fidelity also left Indian retail MF by selling. BlackRock later came back as a 50:50 partner in JioBlackRock (2023). That fits its stated reason, which was a wish for control or integration and not for less exposure to India.
verdicts.denialFound: Nothing needs denying. The stated reason is BlackRock's own account, attributed in the source: "BlackRock said it sold its stake in the joint venture because it could not integrate DSP BlackRock onto its technology and operating platform since it was a minority stakeholder. 'However, India remains a strategic market for BlackRock globally,' said Anthony Arthur, a spokesperson for BlackRock." (https://www.business-standard.com/article/reuters/blackrock-exits-mutual-fund-venture-with-dsp-group-118050701042_1.html). I found no contrary reporting.
verdicts.innocentReading: This was a routine portfolio decision. A 40% minority holder that could not put the JV on its Aladdin/operating platform sold to the 60% partner at a disclosed $40m pre-tax gain. It re-entered India later through a 50:50 JV with Jio. Nothing suggests wrongdoing, and the claim alleges none.
verdicts.reason: The fact holds and upgrades. The cited Reuters/BS article says exactly what the text says: 40%, sold to DSP Group, 7 May 2018, stated reason "could not integrate ... since it was a minority stakeholder". A primary record also confirms it: BlackRock's SEC 10-Q for Q3 2018 and 10-K for FY2018 record the August 2018 completion, the 40% stake, the buyer "The DSP Group" and a $40m pre-tax gain. The edge as encoded is still false and must not be published as it stands. pred=own with s=cap:blackrock and t=cap:dsp-group, from=2018-05-07 and to=null, asserts that BlackRock has owned DSP Group since May 2018. That misstates the direction, the entity owned and the ownership window. I refute the encoding, not the event. Re-encode it and publish at the documented tier.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: Jio Financial Services filed an MF sponsor application with SEBI on 19 Oct 2023. JFS existed as a listed entity from Aug 2023, and its JV with BlackRock was announced in Jul 2023, so the filing date falls after both. The BS article of 3 Jan 2024 says: "Jio Financial, which has a joint venture (JV) with Blackrock Financial Management for asset management, filed the application for MF licence on October 19, 2023." The record's "to" date of 2024-10-04 is one day late. BS of 4 Oct 2024 quotes JFS's own filing: "Sebi, vide letter dated October 3, 2024, has granted in-principle approval to the company and BlackRock Financial Management Inc to act as co-sponsors". The pending-application window therefore closes on 2024-10-03, and the 4th is the day it was disclosed.
verdicts.identityTest: The source names "Jio Financial Services" as the entity on SEBI's updated list of MF applicants, which matches co:jio-financial-services. The claim leaves one thing out. SEBI's later letter and JFS's exchange disclosure show the application was for JFS and BlackRock Financial Management Inc to act together as co-sponsors, so JFS was not the only sponsor. The BS article itself frames the filing as JFS's and places it in the context of the BlackRock JV. The t-node "sebi" is correct.
verdicts.baseRate: Every MF sponsor has to file this application under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations 1996, so all comparable entities share the property. It tells you nothing about any one company, and the claim implies no wrongdoing. The fleet control, Bajaj Finserv (applied Sep 2020; c038), is recorded the same way with the same kind of source. Abira Securities and Angel One sit on the same SEBI list at the same date. The treatment is symmetric.
verdicts.denialFound: Not applicable: the claim is a neutral procedural fact and nothing in it needs denying. The party concerned confirmed the application process in its own exchange disclosure of Oct 2024 (the in-principle approval to JFS and BlackRock as co-sponsors). I found no contrary reporting on the date.
verdicts.innocentReading: This is the ordinary regulatory step for entering the MF business, taken after the JV announcement of Jul 2023. It is a routine regulatory filing and needs no innocent reading beyond that.
verdicts.reason: The one cited source (BS, 3 Jan 2024, Abhishek Kumar, based on SEBI's quarterly applicant list) says exactly what the claim says: the actor is JFS, the regulator is SEBI and the date is 19 Oct 2023. Wider search found other reports repeating the date, but I could not open them to check. "Reported" is the right tier: one credible outlet citing a published regulator document. It moves to "documented" once SEBI's applicant-status list is opened directly, as the record's upgradeIf says. The claim is not refuted. The only problems are small: BlackRock is left out as co-applicant, and the end date is off by one day.
verdicts.corrections: (1) Change text/lab to: "JFS, with BlackRock Financial Management Inc as co-sponsor, filed its MF sponsor application with SEBI on 19 Oct 2023 (SEBI applicant list via BS)". (2) Change "to" from 2024-10-04 to 2024-10-03, the date of SEBI's in-principle letter per the JFS disclosure quoted by BS on 4 Oct 2024. Make the same fix in c039's "in-principle 2024-10-04", which should read 2024-10-03 (then 11.5 months holds approximately). (3) Optionally add as a second source the BS in-principle article: https://www.business-standard.com/markets/mutual-fund/sebi-gives-in-principle-nod-to-jio-blackrock-for-mutual-fund-entry-124100401163_1.html

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: Jio BlackRock Asset Management's three debut NFOs (overnight, liquid, money market) raised Rs 17,800 crore, 30 Jun to 2 Jul 2025. Business Standard (Abhishek Kumar, 7 Jul 2025, 10:56 PM IST) quotes the company release: "The three-day NFO, which was launched on 30 June 2025, attracted investments from over 90 institutional investors". The dates are consistent with the entity's life: SEBI in-principle approval came on 4 Oct 2024 and final MF approval in May 2025, both per BS, so the NFO falls after the licence. verdicts.identityTest: The source names "Jio BlackRock Asset Management", "a 50:50 joint venture between Jio Financial Services (JFS) and BlackRock", headed by MD and CEO Sid Swaminathan. That is the same entity as node s, and JFS is correctly identified. However the money did not go to the AMC or to JFS. It went into the schemes of JioBlackRock Mutual Fund, a SEBI-registered trust, with the AMC as manager. The edge as built, pmin s=cap:jio-blackrock-asset-management to t=co:jio-financial-services, reads under CONTRACT direction rules ("money flows s->t") as money flowing from the AMC to JFS. That is false, and the record's own `d` field disclaims it ("not as JFS revenue"). Attributing the result to JFS alone also drops the other 50% sponsor, BlackRock.
verdicts.baseRate: Non-discriminating as a signal of anything beyond commercial success. Every new AMC launches with NFOs, and debt, liquid and overnight debuts routinely draw institutional treasury money. The size is unusual. Per BS of 13 Aug 2025, citing July NFO data, it drove a record Rs 30,416 cr July NFO mop-up, above the Aug 2021 high of Rs 22,769 cr. Liquid Fund took Rs 8,917 cr and Money Market Rs 6,285 cr (Morningstar's Nehal Meshram). The size is unusual, but it is not evidence of preference or impropriety. On symmetry, the same lens applied to other recent AMC debuts, or to other BlackRock or Vanguard JVs, would record their NFO totals the same way. The SPEC control ("BlackRock never recorded alone") is not breached, since the edge names the JFS side. If anything it omits BlackRock.
verdicts.denialFound: Not applicable. This is the company's own claim, made in its release; there is nothing to deny. No contrary reporting was found. Independent corroboration exists: BS on 13 Aug 2025 (July NFO data, analyst-quoted) repeats Rs 17,800 cr and gives a scheme-wise split. BusinessToday on 7 Jul 2025 carries the same figures from the release.
verdicts.innocentReading: A new, well-capitalised AMC launched cash-management schemes, and corporate treasuries and 67,000+ retail investors parked short-term money in them. Debt NFOs are low-risk parking vehicles, so large institutional tickets are normal. One point is unknown: part of the institutional money may come from Reliance or JFS group treasuries. The source does not name the 90+ institutions, and the record should not imply either way.
verdicts.reason: The source opened (HTTP 200). It states the amount (Rs 17,800 crore), the dates (three-day NFO from 30 June 2025), the counts (over 90 institutional and over 67,000 retail investors) and the rankings (top 35 of 47 by AUM, top 15 by debt AUM), all attributed to a company release. A second BS piece built on July 2025 NFO data corroborates the total. The fact survives. Tier "reported" is correct for a company self-report carried by one outlet. It could move to documented once the AMFI July 2025 monthly NFO data or a JFS exchange intimation is opened directly. The defect is in the edge structure, not the fact. The s->t direction asserts money flowing from the AMC to JFS, which no source says.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Fix the direction: pmin should run from the investors (e.g. an aggregate node "NFO subscribers") to the fund, i.e. t=cap:jio-blackrock-mutual-fund (or cap:jio-blackrock-asset-management as manager). It should not run AMC -> co:jio-financial-services. Carry the JFS link as a separate `own` edge, co:jio-financial-services -> cap:jio-blackrock-asset-management with 50% in d, plus a parallel BlackRock `own` 50% edge for symmetry. 2) Add a second source: https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/jio-blackrock-debut-powers-record-july-inflows-in-mutual-fund-nfos-125081301187_1.html (13 Aug 2025; July NFO mop-up Rs 30,416 cr, including JioBlackRock Rs 17,800 cr; Liquid Rs 8,917 cr, Money Market Rs 6,285 cr). 3) Add to d: "institutional investors not named in source; group-treasury share unknown." 4) Keep upgradeIf as it is (the AMFI July 2025 monthly note, or the JFSL BSE/NSE intimation of 7 Jul 2025).

verdicts.identityTest: The entity matches. The cited BS article says: "Jio BlackRock Broking Pvt Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of Jio BlackRock Investment Advisers Pvt Ltd, has received regulatory approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) to commence operations as a brokerage firm." verdicts.identityTest: The entities match the sources. BS 27 May 2025 says "Jio BlackRock Asset Management (AMC) has received the final approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India... The company had received in-principle approval from Sebi for the MF foray on 4 October 2024." BS 3 Jan 2024 says JFS "filed the application for MF licence on October 19, 2023." verdicts.baseRate:
The file uses n=2 (Jio vs Bajaj). The fair comparison is the 2023–25 cohort, and it does not single out Jio BlackRock.
(1) In-principle leg. Capitalmind, an unconnected Bengaluru PMS firm, was in the same queue as Jio at 30 Jun 2024 (BS 26 Aug 2024: "three other applicants were in the fray for in-principle approval as of June 30. These companies included the Jio Financial and BlackRock Financial joint venture..."). Capitalmind got its in-principle approval on 26 Aug 2024, five-plus weeks before Jio's on 4 Oct 2024. Jio had filed earlier (19 Oct 2023), so it was overtaken in the queue. Search snippets give Capitalmind's application date as 5 Jan 2024, which would make its in-principle leg about 7.7 months against Jio's 11.5. I did not open a page confirming that date.
(2) Final leg. Capitalmind went from 26 Aug 2024 to final approval announced on 14 Apr 2025 (BS 14 Apr 2025), about 7.5 months. Jio took 7.7 months. Angel One took about 21 months (in-principle Feb 2023, CoR 25 Nov 2024) and Unifi about 12 months (in-principle Nov 2023, final Nov 2024), per BS 16 Jul 2024 and 26 Nov 2024.
So Jio ties the fastest unconnected peer on the final leg and trails it on the in-principle leg. The "7.7 vs 19 months" gap in strongestCase comes from choosing a pre-speed-up control, not from anything specific to Jio.
verdicts.denialFound: None found. I did not find any named party making the fast-track allegation against Jio BlackRock or SEBI. Searches for favouritism or fast-track criticism returned only approval coverage. SEBI and JFS have not been asked, and there is no response on record. Their release (BS 27 May 2025) makes no comment on timing.
verdicts.innocentReading: SEBI shortened MF licence timelines for every applicant from 2023. BS 3 Jan 2024 says "Lately, Sebi has quickened licence approvals... The queue for licence has also shortened due to changes in net-worth criteria." BS 7 Jan 2025 reports several partial and final approvals in a few months and says "Sebi inspects the progress after six months. The final licence is issued if the applicant meets all the criteria." Jio BlackRock's roughly 7.7-month final leg is that six-month inspection plus about a month and a half, the same as Capitalmind. A well-capitalised JV with a global co-sponsor that had already hired its CEO and CIO would be expected to finish at the fast end of the standard window. The separate IA and broking registrations are routine processes, and they also followed the JV's own schedule.
verdicts.reason: The sources say what the file says, but the narrative's status of "contested" overstates the fast-track case. The only support for it is an n=2 comparison against a control from before the speed-up. In the actual 2024–25 cohort, drawn from BS articles I opened, the unconnected applicant Capitalmind got its in-principle approval before Jio despite filing later, and it cleared the final leg in the same time (about 7.5 vs 7.7 months). Angel One and Unifi were slower. The one timing fact the narrative relies on therefore does not discriminate. The status should be "not supported by the timeline evidence", not "contested". The analytic tier is right for a narrative built from our own comparison.
