verdicts.dateTest: Claim: Hindenburg Research published its Adani report on 24 Jan 2023. Hindenburg operated from 2017 until it closed in Jan 2025, so the report falls inside that window. The page shows "Published on January 24, 2023" and an update date of "February 5, 2023". The claim's "from": "2023-01-24" is correct. The supersession date is also consistent: SEBI's order of 2025-09-18 (c009) comes after the report.
verdicts.identityTest: The actor is energy:hindenburg, Hindenburg Research, the US short-seller. The report names itself as "Hindenburg Research". The target is grp:adani, and the report does target the group: "the INR 17.8 trillion (U.S. $218 billion) Indian conglomerate Adani Group" and its 7 listed companies. The target is a corporate group, not a family, so the family-framing kill does not apply. Vinod Adani is named in the description only. One identity problem: pred "enforce" is defined in CONTRACT.md as "agency → subject: cancellation, suspension, freeze, investigation, sanction, debarment". Hindenburg is a private short-seller, not an agency, and a research report is not an enforcement action, so the predicate misdescribes what kind of actor this is. energy/enforce.json c001 records the same event with the same pattern.
verdicts.baseRate: Every activist short report states that the author holds a short position; the report says the same about itself ("Hindenburg Research ... has a short position in all stocks or bonds ... covered herein"). So the disclosed short says nothing about whether this report is accurate. It only establishes the benefit, which the record already captures. Symmetry: a short-seller's allegation stays at tier alleged whatever the target is, whether Nikola, Icahn or Adani. That is the right treatment and it is applied evenly. Nothing in this record depends on UPA vs NDA or on the BlackRock/Vanguard controls.
verdicts.denialFound: Adani Group denied the allegations. c002 cites Adani's 31 Aug 2023 statement to OCCRP ("baseless and unsubstantiated", "rehashed from Hindenburg's allegations", https://www.occrp.org/en/investigation/documents-provide-fresh-insight-into-allegations-of-stock-manipulation-that-rocked-indias-powerful-adani-group) and its Aug 2024 statement (https://www.newsonair.gov.in/adani-group-and-industry-leaders-condemn-hindenburg-report-defend-sebi-chairpersons-integrity). The direct response to this report, the 413-page rebuttal of 29 Jan 2023, was not opened by the author. I could not open it either: a guessed adani.com URL returned 404, and the web-search budget was used up. So the contra exists, but for this specific report it is indirect. The adjudicated response is SEBI's 18 Sep 2025 order (c009), which found the Milestone/Rehvar allegations "not established".
verdicts.innocentReading: The boring explanation also fits: the edge records only that a short-seller holding a position published allegations on that date, and that is exactly what the source shows. For the substance, the innocent reading is Adani's: the offshore holders were independent investors, and the flagged loans were ordinary commercial loans repaid with interest. SEBI accepted that reading for the Milestone/Rehvar loans (c009). SEBI has not issued an order on the FPI beneficial-ownership or stock-manipulation strand, so the innocent reading is established for two strands and neither confirmed nor refuted for the core.
verdicts.reason:
The source checks out. I opened https://hindenburgresearch.com/adani/ (curl, 440 KB), and it matches the claim on every point:
- Charge: "Adani Group has engaged in a brazen stock manipulation and accounting fraud scheme over the course of decades".
- Shells: "We have identified 38 Mauritius shell entities controlled by Vinod Adani or close associates".
- Short position: "we have taken a short position in Adani Group Companies through U.S.-traded bonds and non-Indian-traded derivative instruments".
- Liquidity: "5 of 7 key listed companies have reported 'current ratios' below 1".
- Questions: "We have included 88 questions".
- The Milestone Tradelinks, Rehvar and Adicorp strands that SEBI later decided are in the report.

Tier alleged is right for a short-seller's unadjudicated claim, and a contra is attached. So the edge itself holds.

What fails is the supersession link. c009 is SEBI's order on the Milestone/Rehvar related-party-transaction strand, plus a companion order on Adicorp. That is two of the 24 investigations, and c009's own text says it "is not a finding on the FPI beneficial-ownership strand". The lead of this claim, "stock manipulation ... via 38 Mauritius shells", is exactly that FPI strand. Saying the whole report is "superseded by SEBI 2025 order c009" combines two true facts into a conclusion neither supports. It reproduces the mirror narrative the file itself lists ("SEBI's 2025 orders prove Hindenburg false"). The claim survives as an alleged edge, but the supersededBy field and the predicate have to be fixed.
verdicts.corrections:
1. supersededBy: change "narratives-literature:c009" to null. Under CONTRACT §3, supersession needs a newer fact on the same thing, and c009 answers only the Milestone/Rehvar (and companion Adicorp) strands. Put the partial answer in d instead: "Two strands (Milestone/Rehvar; Adicorp) closed 'not established' by SEBI on 2025-09-18 (c009); FPI beneficial-ownership / stock-manipulation strand not adjudicated as of the record date."
2. text/lab: replace "superseded by SEBI 2025 order c009 (two RPT strands 'not established')" with "partially answered by SEBI 2025 order c009 (two RPT strands 'not established'; the Mauritius-FPI strand is open)".
3. lab: "stock manipulation and accounting fraud via 38 Mauritius shells" puts both charges on the Mauritius entities. The report names 38 Mauritius shells plus entities in Cyprus, the UAE, Singapore and the Caribbean, and the accounting-fraud charge rests largely on undisclosed related-party loans (Milestone, Rehvar, Adicorp). Suggested wording: "stock manipulation and accounting fraud; offshore network incl. 38 Mauritius shells tied to Vinod Adani".
4. pred: "enforce" is defined as agency → subject, and Hindenburg is not an agency. Either take this up at the contract level (there is no predicate for a private allegation) or mark the edge in d as "allegation, not enforcement". Apply the same fix to energy/enforce.json c001, which has the same problem. That record also does not link to its SEBI order claim (c005), so the two files are inconsistent.
5. c002 (contra): its "from" is 2023-01-29, but its sources are from Aug 2023 and Aug 2024. Either open and cite Adani's 29 Jan 2023 rebuttal or set from to 2023-08-31.
6. killIf: fine as written. Keep upgradeIf pointed at the FPI beneficial-ownership strand, which is still open.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim as written: OCCRP (with the Guardian and FT) published on 31 Aug 2023 that Ahli and Chang held Adani stock via EIFF/EMRF, peaking at $430m in March 2017, with trades from 2013 to 2018. The OCCRP page is dated "August 31, 2023". The 2011 Excel agreement signed by Vinod Adani, the $1.4m in Excel fees (Jun 2012 to Aug 2014) and the 2014 DRI letter all fall inside or before the 2013–2018 trading window. Nothing is anachronistic. from=2023-08-31 is the publication date, which fits an allegation edge. The record is stale for asOf 2026-09-26, though: (a) OCCRP followed up on 17 Feb 2026 ("Bank Documents Expose Scale of Secret Investments…"), reporting about $3bn held via Reyl MEA as recently as 2023, and a Swiss federal criminal probe into Chang with $310m frozen under an Aug 2024 ruling. (b) Reuters, Business Standard and ET reported on 24 Aug 2026 that SEBI rejected settlement applications from 13 Adani-linked foreign funds, so the FPI strand is still open and killIf is not met. (c) SEBI's Sept 2025 clean-chit orders covered other strands, not this one.
verdicts.identityTest: The actors match the source. OCCRP names "Nasser Ali Shaban Ahli and Chang Chung-Ling", the funds "Emerging India Focus Fund (EIFF) and EM Resurgent Fund (EMRF)" and "Excel Investment and Advisory Services Limited". The node has two problems. Its id is 'energy:occrp' (energy namespace) inside a capital file, and its ty is 'company', although OCCRP is a US 501(c)(3) newsroom. The predicate is also wrong. 'enforce' is defined in CONTRACT as agency → subject (cancellation, suspension, freeze, investigation, sanction, debarment), and OCCRP is not an agency. Recording OCCRP→Adani as 'enforce' in the same file that documents OCCRP's USG/OSF funding sets up exactly the conjunction the SPEC warns about: funder → OCCRP → 'enforcement' against Adani, read as coordination. The real actors (Ahli, Chang, EIFF, EMRF, Excel, Vinod Adani) are not nodes. "Adani family" here means the promoter group, a legal category under SEBI rules made up of named individuals, not an ethnic or religious framing. The edge target grp:adani is an institution, so there is no bloodline problem.
verdicts.baseRate: Concentrated FPI holdings are common. SEBI's 2023 granular-disclosure rules captured about 40 business groups with concentrated FPI holdings, including the Tatas and Hindujas (Moneycontrol, 18 Jul 2023). So "Mauritius FPIs hold a lot of group X stock" alone does not discriminate. What does discriminate is specific to this case and documented by OCCRP: an advisory agreement signed by the promoter's brother (2011), $1.4m in fees paid to a Vinod Adani-owned adviser, both investors serving as directors of Vinod Adani companies, and Vinod Adani investing through the same GOF/EIFF chain. Symmetry: SEBI's FPI look-through rules apply the same test to every group, and no group comparable to Adani has an alleged promoter-signed adviser agreement on record. The claim is not an artefact of lens selection.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes. OCCRP, 31 Aug 2023, quoting an Adani representative: "these allegations are not only baseless and unsubstantiated but are rehashed from Hindenburg's allegations… all the Adani Group's publicly listed entities are in compliance with all applicable laws including the regulation relating to public share holdings" (recorded as c004). Ahli and Chang did not respond to OCCRP. Chang told the Guardian he knew nothing about secret purchases: "We are a simple business." OCCRP, 17 Feb 2026: an Adani spokesperson said the alleged "front men" are "public shareholders", and in a Feb 2023 written statement to their bank Ahli and Chang denied wrongdoing. The SC in Vishal Tiwari v UoI (3 Jan 2024, para 40) said: "reliance on newspaper articles or reports by third-party organizations to question a comprehensive investigation by a specialized regulator does not inspire confidence" (c007, confirmed at https://indiankanoon.org/doc/188573380/). Sources: https://www.occrp.org/en/investigation/documents-provide-fresh-insight-into-allegations-of-stock-manipulation-that-rocked-indias-powerful-adani-group ; https://www.occrp.org/en/investigation/bank-documents-expose-scale-of-secret-investments-in-adani-group-by-adani-family-associates
verdicts.innocentReading: Ahli and Chang are long-standing independent business associates who invested their own money in Adani stock because, in their words to their bank, they "had personal and business relationships with the family and trusted their business acumen". Excel's advisory role would then be ordinary fund advice rather than control. OCCRP itself says "There is no evidence that Chang and Ahli's money for their Adani Group investments came from the Adani family. The source of the funds is unknown." Under this reading the holdings are public float and the 75% cap is not breached. It stays open until SEBI or a court decides whether the two acted in concert with the promoters.
verdicts.reason: The source says what the claim says. The quoted text reads: "In at least two cases — representing Adani stock holdings that at one point reached $430 million — the mysterious investors turn out to have widely reported ties to… the Adani family"; "At one point in March 2017, the value of the investments in Adani Group stock was $430 million"; "An agreement for Excel to provide advisory services to EIFF and EMRF was signed for Excel by Vinod Adani himself in 2011". The date, actors, amount and funds all match, and the ₹ figure is a labelled approximation. The claim carries two contras (Adani's denial, and the SC's holding on evidentiary weight), and the central legal question, whether the two acted for the promoters, has not been decided. SEBI rejected the funds' settlement bids in Aug 2026, so the FPI strand is still open. 'alleged' is the right tier for the edge's thrust. 'reported' would fit only the bare holding facts, and the "instructions" element rests on a single unnamed source. Guardian and FT co-published from shared documents, so they are not independent outlets and do not lift the tier to documented. The claim survives on substance but needs structural fixes: the predicate and the node.
verdicts.corrections: 1) The pred 'enforce' is wrong because OCCRP is not an agency. Either model the underlying fact as an 'own' edge (EIFF/EMRF, with Ahli/Chang as beneficial holders → Adani listed companies, tier alleged, src OCCRP), or keep this as a narrative with OCCRP as publisher in 'srcs' only, not as edge source 's'. Do not leave an OCCRP→grp:adani edge that reads as enforcement. 2) Rename the node 'energy:occrp' to the capital namespace (e.g. 'capital:occrp') and change ty from 'company' to the nearest allowed non-profit type, noting the US 501(c)(3) status in 'sub'. 3) Text: replace "taking instructions through a Vinod Adani-linked adviser" with "which, per an unnamed source, took instructions from Excel Investment and Advisory Services, whose 2011 advisory agreement Vinod Adani signed and which received $1.4m in fees (2012–14)". 4) 'srcs' cites only OCCRP while the text credits the Guardian and FT. Either add the Guardian/FT 31 Aug 2023 URLs or say "OCCRP (shared with Guardian/FT)", and note they are not independent. 5) 'd' quotes the 2014 DRI letter but leaves out that the DRI over-valuation case was later set aside (DRI adjudication, CESTAT, SC; OCCRP itself says "Both cases were eventually dismissed"). Add that. 6) Amount: state US$430m as the primary figure (March 2017 peak value, not the amount invested). ₹2,795 cr at ₹65/$ is fine as approximate, since the March 2017 RBI reference rate ran from about 66.7 down to 64.84. 7) Add a supersede/update edge for OCCRP 17 Feb 2026 (about $3bn held via Reyl MEA as of 2023; Swiss federal prosecutor's money-laundering/forgery probe into Chang, $310m frozen), and record SEBI's Aug 2026 rejection of settlement bids by 13 Adani-linked FPIs (Reuters/Business Standard/ET, 24 Aug 2026) against killIf. killIf is not triggered, and the FPI strand stays open.

verdicts.dateTest: Restated as: Hindenburg published allegations against Madhabi Puri Buch on 10 Aug 2024. The Buch conduct it describes falls in these windows. (1) IPE Plus Fund 1 account opened 5 Jun 2015. She was not at SEBI then; she became Whole-Time Member in Apr 2017. (2) Dhaval Buch's email to Trident Trust asking to be "the sole person authorised to operate the Accounts" is dated 22 Mar 2017, "just weeks ahead of" her WTM appointment. (3) Account statement dated 26 Feb 2018, stake "U.S. $872,762.25 at the time". Redemption email dated 25 Feb 2018, while she was WTM. (4) Agora Partners shares moved to her husband on 16 Mar 2022, "two weeks after her appointment as SEBI Chairperson" (2 Mar 2022). (5) Agora Advisory revenue in FY2022. (6) Dhaval Buch joined Blackstone as Senior Advisor in Jul 2019. The tenures line up with the source. One date in the record is wrong: the d field says Dhaval Buch "sought sole operating authority in Mar 2022". The source says 22 Mar 2017.
verdicts.identityTest: The nodes match the source. energy:madhabi-puri-buch is the SEBI WTM (Apr 2017 to 2021) and Chairperson (from 2 Mar 2022) that the report names. The funds are named in the source: "GDOF Cell 90 (IPEplus Fund 1)" (Mauritius), the Bermuda Global Dynamic Opportunities Fund, and IIFL, "now called 360 One". So are the companies: Agora Partners Pte Ltd (Singapore, registered 27 Mar 2013) and Agora Advisory Private Limited (India, incorporated 7 May 2013, 99% hers). One weakness is that the fund and account facts rest on "whistleblower documents", which Hindenburg did not publish in full. However, the Buchs' own 11 Aug 2024 statement admits the 2015 investment and the 2018 redemption, so the identity of the holding is not in dispute.
verdicts.baseRate: I found no published data on how many senior SEBI officials held offshore feeder-fund units or consulting firms before appointment, so I cannot compute a base rate. The general features are weak discriminators. Offshore fund holdings by Singapore-resident professionals (the Buchs lived in Singapore in 2015), consulting companies owned by a spouse, and a spouse advising a large PE firm are all common among senior finance professionals. What discriminates is specific to this case: the same GDOF/IPE Plus cell that Hindenburg says Vinod Adani used, and the timing of the transfers around her appointments. The one-sided claim that Adani money sat in this cell comes from Hindenburg and Adani Watch. The Buchs say the fund never invested in any Adani security. Symmetry: the edge records a short-seller's allegation about a regulator. The same lens applied to any SEBI chair, under UPA or NDA, would record allegations against them the same way, with the same tier and the same contra requirement. The claim does not frame a family, religion or ethnicity as the actor.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, denials exist. The Buchs issued a joint statement on 10 Aug 2024 calling the allegations "baseless" (The Hindu: https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/sebi-chief-madhabi-buch-husband-deny-hindenburg-allegations-as-baseless/article68510890.ece). A detailed rebuttal followed on 11 Aug 2024. It says the investment was made in 2015 "almost 2 years before Madhabi joined SEBI", that it was redeemed in 2018 when CIO Anil Ahuja left the fund, and that "at no point in time did the fund invest in any bond, equity, or derivative of any Adani group company". It also says the Agora companies went dormant on her appointment (Livemint: https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-market-news/hindenburgadani-case-sebi-chief-madhabi-puri-and-husband-dhaval-buch-respond-to-allegations-attempting-to-attack-11723375754189.html). AMFI and others issued supporting statements on 12 Aug 2024 (newsonair; this is c014, from the state broadcaster). On 28 May 2025 the Lokpal dismissed three complaints as vexatious, finding them "more on presumptions and assumptions and not supported by any verifiable material" (LiveLaw; c013). The contra edges c012 and c014 are present, so the rule that alleged claims must carry a contra is met.
verdicts.innocentReading: The Buchs were private citizens in Singapore in 2015. They invested savings in a fund run by a friend (Anil Ahuja, ex-IIFL CIO) and redeemed it in 2018 when he left. On their account the fund held no Adani securities. The move to Dhaval Buch's sole control in 2017 and the Agora share transfer in 2022 were routine steps to distance her from her holdings on taking public office. Agora Advisory's revenue came from Dhaval Buch's own consulting. His Blackstone role came from his supply-chain expertise, and SEBI's recusal framework covered any overlap. The Lokpal found no prima facie case. Nothing in hand shows that any SEBI decision on Adani or REITs was affected.
verdicts.reason: The source at https://hindenburgresearch.com/sebi/ (fetched, HTTP 200) says what the edge's text says. Hindenburg on 10 Aug 2024 alleged Buch-linked stakes in "GDOF Cell 90 (IPEplus Fund 1)" and the Bermuda GDOF, run by IIFL/360 One, the same structure it says Vinod Adani used. It also alleged the Agora Partners transfer "two weeks after her appointment as SEBI Chairperson", Agora Advisory revenue of "INR 19.8 million (U.S. $261,000)", and a Blackstone/REIT conflict. The report cites "whistleblower documents". Its disclaimer covers short positions, and it says "any proceeds... will be donated to causes that support free expression". As a record that a named party made an allegation, the edge holds, and alleged is the right tier. It carries contra c012 and c014 and the Lokpal dismissal c013. It should not be upgraded, because no authority has found any wrongdoing. It should not be killed either: the Lokpal order rejects a corruption case but does not show that the allegation was never made. The Buchs themselves admit the underlying holding. The edge is not refuted, but the record contains a factual date error and a conversion error. Its predicate also breaks the contract, which defines enforce as agency to subject, and Hindenburg is not an agency. The rest of the fleet uses the same convention for Hindenburg edges.
verdicts.corrections: 1. d field, date error: "that Dhaval Buch sought sole operating authority in Mar 2022" should read "on 22 Mar 2017, weeks before her Apr 2017 appointment as SEBI Whole-Time Member, Dhaval Buch asked Trident Trust to make him 'the sole person authorised to operate the Accounts'". The source says 22 Mar 2017. 2. d field, amount: Agora Advisory's FY2022 revenue is given in rupees by the source as INR 19.8 million, which is Rs 1.98 crore, not "≈ Rs 2.1 crore". Use the source's rupee figure instead of a converted one. 3. d field: add that the $872,762.25 value comes from an account statement dated 26 Feb 2018, and that the redemption request came on 25 Feb 2018, during her WTM tenure. 4. d field: the short-position line comes from Hindenburg's boilerplate disclaimer ("you should assume... has a short position"), not a specific disclosure. Reword it that way. 5. supersededBy / text framing: "superseded by Lokpal dismissal c013" overstates the case. The Lokpal dismissed corruption complaints as lacking verifiable material. It did not show the allegation was never made, and the Buchs admit the fund holding. Record c013 as contra/adjudication rather than supersession, or keep supersededBy but add in d that the admitted facts (2015 investment, 2018 redemption) survive. 6. Predicate: CONTRACT defines enforce as "agency → subject". Hindenburg is a short-seller, not an agency. Flag this as a fleet-wide convention issue (the same usage appears in enforce:c010, lit:c020 and narratives-literature:c001) instead of fixing this one edge alone. 7. c012 date: the Buchs' first denial was issued on the evening of 10 Aug 2024, with the detailed statement on 11 Aug. Add The Hindu and Livemint as sources to c012, alongside the newsonair and LiveLaw links, which are only secondary sources for the denial.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: US federal government (USAID/State Dept) funded OCCRP for 2008–2023, and Drop Site plus partners reported it on 2 Dec 2024. The "from" date of 2024-12-02 matches the publication date Drop Site gives. The funding windows (2014–2023 for the 52%, since 2008 for US$47m, 2016 for 63%) fall inside OCCRP's existence (founded 2008) and match the source. The key-personnel remark is present tense, from USAID's Meg Gaydosik in 2024. No anachronism.
verdicts.identityTest: The node energy:occrp is the Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project, which is the entity both sources name. The funder is the "American federal government" (mainly USAID and the State Department). The claim text's "US government" is accurate. The named USAID official is Meg Gaydosik and the chief of party is Drew Sullivan, both matching the source. One co-publisher is misidentified: the record's `d` lists NDR among the publishers, but Drop Site says NDR "has not published its own version of the investigation" after "pressure from the organization." The outlets that published were Drop Site, Mediapart, Il Fatto Quotidiano and Reporters United.
verdicts.baseRate: Having the US or other Western governments as the largest funder is typical of investigative-journalism non-profits working in the post-Soviet and Balkan region, where there is little local philanthropy. Examples are RFE/RL (almost entirely US-funded), BIRN, and many IREX/USAID and NED media grantees. So the property is probably shared by most of that peer group and does not single out OCCRP. The claim only describes the funding, though. It does not say US funding caused any particular story, so the base rate limits what can be inferred rather than refuting the fact. On symmetry, the same lens applied to a donor-funded outlet aligned with the Indian government would give the same "funder share" reading. Nothing in the claim is framed by family, religion or ethnicity.
verdicts.denialFound: OCCRP's response appears in the Drop Site piece: restrictions like these "are common across all government grants" and "no donor has ever vetoed any staff position." Drew Sullivan disputed the method and put the figure at 46.4% after excluding pass-through grants. The OCCRP FAQ (https://www.occrp.org/en/frequently-asked-questions-on-occrps-funding-and-editorial-policies, updated 7 Dec 2024) says "Donors never have access to editorial meetings or any aspect of our editorial process, nor do they have input into what stories we publish." The same FAQ admits the substance of the key-personnel point: "the donor needs to agree that the replacement is qualified." The State Department denied influencing editorial decisions (ThePrint, 7 Dec 2024). OCCRP was asked before publication, and its denial is recorded as c017.
verdicts.innocentReading: Western governments are the main funders of cross-border investigative non-profits in regions without domestic philanthropy. Standard US federal cooperative agreements require the grantor to approve changes to named key personnel (2 CFR 200.308). Neither fact shows that a government commissioned or steered any story.
verdicts.reason: I could not refute the claim. The primary source (Drop Site, 2 Dec 2024) states each element nearly word for word: "Between 2014 and 2023, the American federal government provided 52 percent of the money actually spent by OCCRP"; Sullivan's own method gives 46.4%; "Since its founding in 2008, has shoveled at least $47 million"; and Gaydosik says "we review it and say, okay... we approve your nominee for a new chief of party." OCCRP's own FAQ confirms the donor's sign-off on key personnel, and its "46%" is OCCRP's own figure, so the party concerned partly corroborates the claim. The tier stays at reported, not documented, because this is one joint consortium investigation (the co-publishers are not independent of each other) and OCCRP has not published a funder-by-funder audit showing the 52%. The claim is descriptive and pairs it with the c017 contra, so it does not suggest any link to editorial content.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Currency conversion error in `d`: US$47m × Rs 84 = Rs 394.8 crore, not "Rs 3,950 crore". That is a tenfold crore error; change it to "≈ Rs 395 crore". 2) Remove NDR from the list of publishers in `d`. Drop Site says NDR did not publish its version under pressure from OCCRP. The publishers were Drop Site, Mediapart, Il Fatto Quotidiano and Reporters United. 3) Specify "46.4% (Sullivan's method, excluding pass-through sub-grants)" rather than an unexplained "46% on OCCRP's basis". 4) The "≥US$47m" figure covers 2008 to 2024 publication, with a further US$12m committed; add "plus $12m committed". 5) The OCCRP FAQ source supports only the key-personnel approval and the denial, not the percentages. Its role could be noted in the claim, or it could be left under c017 only. 6) The predicate is odd: a reported funding fact is recorded as pred "analytic" from a document node. Consider recording the underlying flow as a `grant` edge from USAID/US government to energy:occrp (a ≈ 394.8 crore, cumulative 2008–2024, tier reported), with the Drop Site document as its source.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: BJP (Smriti Irani) accused Soros of seeking regime change, 17 Feb 2023. The dates line up. Soros spoke at the Munich Security Conference on Thursday 16 Feb 2023, and Irani replied the next day. She was Union Minister for Women and Child Development at the time (2019–2024) and spoke to reporters at the BJP office. The article is dated 17 Feb 2023.
verdicts.identityTest: Fails on the target. Irani named George Soros the person: "A foreign power at the centre of which is a man named George Soros has announced that he will hurt India's democratic structure..." She did not name Open Society Foundations. Soros spoke at Munich in his own name, not as OSF. The Al Jazeera article never mentions OSF. OSF only enters the story in later reporting (Al Jazeera Dec 2024 calls Soros "the founder of the Open Society Foundation"). So the edge t=cap:open-society-foundations treats the man as his foundation, which the source does not do. The source is also a party, not an agency, so the predicate is wrong.
verdicts.baseRate: Not discriminating as evidence about OSF. The BJP and ministers attacking Soros is a recurring pattern (Feb 2023, then Dec 2024 on FDL-AP and Congress), so one more statement says nothing new about OSF activity. Symmetry: the opposition also distanced itself. Congress's Jairam Ramesh said on 17 Feb 2023 that any democratic revival "has nothing to do with George Soros". So rejecting Soros's remark was not special to the BJP. The claim's own killIf condition is met: no OSF programme aimed at India's government or elections was found, and OSF said in Sept 2023 that its India grants had been restricted since 2016.
verdicts.denialFound: No direct Soros or OSF answer to the Feb 2023 statement was found. OSF was asked: Al Jazeera (26 Dec 2024) "sought responses from Open Society Foundations on the allegations against it levelled by the BJP and ministers in the Modi government but has not yet received a reply" (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/12/26/how-george-soros-became-enemy-number-1-for-indias-modi). The same article quotes OSF's Sept 2023 statement: "Since mid-2016, our grant making in India has been constrained by government restrictions on our funding for local NGOs." So c019's "asked/not asked unknown" is wrong. It should read asked, no reply, plus the Sept 2023 statement on restricted grant-making.
verdicts.innocentReading: A party politician gave a political rebuttal to a foreign billionaire's public prediction about the Prime Minister. It is rhetoric in a press briefing, not a sanction, investigation or any other state action against OSF. Soros's own remark was an opinion ("I may be naive, but I expect a democratic revival in India"), and no funding programme was attached to it.
verdicts.reason: The quotes are accurate: Al Jazeera/Reuters, 17 Feb 2023, has "he talks of regime change" and "A foreign power at the centre of which is a man named George Soros has announced that he will hurt India's democratic structure". But the edge as coded misstates what happened. pred=enforce means agency→subject cancellation, suspension, freeze, investigation or sanction. The BJP is a party, not an agency, and a press-briefing statement is not enforcement. The target is also wrong: the source names George Soros personally and never mentions OSF. As a graph edge, "BJP enforce OSF" suggests an action against OSF that never took place. The fact that the statement was made is documented by several outlets (Reuters/Al Jazeera, Gulf News, Tribune, WION). Its substance, that Soros seeks regime change, is an allegation. That belongs in the narratives array, not as an enforce edge. The linked contra c019 also misstates the response record.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Delete the edge c018 (bjp→cap:open-society-foundations, pred=enforce). 2) Re-record it as a narrative entry, or if the schema requires an edge, as an alleged assertion from bjp (speaker Smriti Irani, Union Minister WCD, BJP HQ press briefing, 17 Feb 2023) aimed at a person node george-soros, not OSF. Do not use pred=enforce. 3) Add a second outlet so the fact of the statement is documented, e.g. https://gulfnews.com/world/asia/india/indias-bjp-slams-soros-for-saying-adanis-troubles-will-weaken-modi-1.93911574 or https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/nation/bid-to-target-indian-democratic-system-govt-ticks-off-us-investor-george-soros-480809. Keep the substance at alleged. 4) Change c019's lab/d to: "Asked, no reply (Al Jazeera, 26 Dec 2024); OSF Sept 2023 statement: grant-making in India constrained since mid-2016 by government restrictions", with src https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/12/26/how-george-soros-became-enemy-number-1-for-indias-modi. 5) Add the symmetry note: Congress (Jairam Ramesh, 17 Feb 2023) also rejected Soros's relevance. 6) Correct d: the Soros speech was 16 Feb 2023 and Irani replied 17 Feb.

verdicts.dateTest: Written as: BJP (Sambit Patra at a party media briefing, plus the BJP's X account) accused OCCRP of being a US State Department / "deep state" media tool meant to destabilise India by targeting Modi, on Thursday 5 Dec 2024. ThePrint (Sakshi Dayal and YP Rajesh, 07 Dec 2024, 01:48 pm IST) says Patra spoke "at an official media briefing by the party on Thursday", which was 5 Dec 2024. The claim's "7 Dec 2024" and from=2024-12-07 are the article's publication date, not the date of the statement. This is a two-day error that can be fixed. Order of events: Mediapart/Drop Site report on OCCRP funding (early Dec 2024), US indictment of Adani (Nov 2024), BJP accusation (5 Dec). The accusation came after the facts it cites, so no chronology problem.
verdicts.identityTest: The node s=bjp is correct: the party is the actor. The label misattributes one quote, though. The only words ThePrint gives to Patra personally are: "A French investigative media group…has revealed that… 50% of OCCRP's funding comes directly from the U.S. State Department. OCCRP has served as a media tool for carrying out a deep state agenda." The phrase "The Deep State had a clear objective to destabilise India by targeting Prime Minister Modi" is attributed to "the BJP said in a series of messages on X", not to Patra. The 'd' field names "Mediapart", but ThePrint only says "a French investigative media group"/"a French media report". Naming Mediapart is our own inference (probably correct, since Mediapart co-published with Drop Site), but the cited source does not say it. The target t=energy:occrp is the right entity. Predicate: CONTRACT defines `enforce` as "agency → subject: cancellation, suspension, freeze, investigation, sanction, debarment". The BJP is a political party, not an agency, and a press-briefing accusation is none of those actions. So the predicate is wrong under the contract, even though the file uses `enforce` for several party accusations (bjp, energy:inc).
verdicts.baseRate: This does not discriminate as evidence about OCCRP. Governing parties calling foreign-funded investigative outlets a "foreign hand" or "deep state" tool is common across regimes (Fidesz on OSF, Russia's "foreign agent" labels, and Indian governments of both parties since Indira Gandhi's "foreign hand" rhetoric). OCCRP's large US-government funding share is openly disclosed and applies to all of its reporting worldwide, not just India. So the funding fact cannot single out the Adani reporting as directed. Symmetry check: the same lens would read any OCCRP story about an opposition-linked or rival-country figure as US-directed too, which shows the lens does no work. As a record of what the party said, the edge is accurate and discriminating: the BJP actually said it.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, in the same article (ThePrint, 7 Dec 2024, https://theprint.in/diplomacy/attempt-to-destabilise-india-bjp-claims-us-state-dept-targeting-country-with-adani-indictment/2392501/). OCCRP: "The U.S. government, while providing some funding to OCCRP, has no say in our editorial processes." US State Department spokesperson: support for journalists "does not influence the editorial decisions or direction of these organizations" and "It's disappointing that the ruling party in India would make these kinds of accusations." Congress and Soros were asked and "did not immediately respond". Hindenburg is not mentioned in the article, so there is no record that it was asked or that it responded.
verdicts.innocentReading: OCCRP does get a large share of its budget from US-government grants. OCCRP says so itself, and the French report the BJP cited confirms it. But it is a pan-regional nonprofit newsroom with many donors, and funding at that level does not show editorial direction of any particular story. The Nov 2024 US indictment of Adani was brought by DOJ/SEC through court process, separate from OCCRP's Aug 2023 reporting. Linking the two is the BJP's inference. The simpler reading is a governing party answering damaging coverage of an allied business group with a foreign-interference frame, as is common.
verdicts.reason: The central record holds: ThePrint, a credible outlet with named sourcing, reports the BJP (Patra at a media briefing plus the party's X posts) calling OCCRP a US State Department "deep state" media tool meant to destabilise India by targeting Modi. As a narrative edge recording what the party said, it survives, and `alleged` is the right tier for its content. It has a real documented contra (c021: OCCRP and the State Department, same article). What does not survive: the statement date (5 Dec, not 7 Dec), the attribution of the "destabilise India by targeting PM Modi" quote to Patra (it came from the BJP's X posts), the "Mediapart" name (not in the source), the `enforce` predicate (the BJP is not an agency and took no enforcement action), and c038 listed as a contra (Hindenburg was not addressed, has no source and made no denial, so it cannot count as a contra). The claim stays, with these corrections.
verdicts.corrections: 1) from: 2024-12-07 -> 2024-12-05 (the Thursday media briefing); keep "ThePrint 7 Dec 2024" as the source label. 2) lab/text: attribute to "BJP (Sambit Patra media briefing and BJP X posts, 5 Dec 2024)". Patra's own quote: "OCCRP has served as a media tool for carrying out a deep state agenda"; "destabilise India by targeting Prime Minister Modi" comes from the BJP's X posts. 3) d: change "(Mediapart)" to "(unnamed in source; 'a French investigative media group')", or add a separate Mediapart/Drop Site source if the name is kept. 4) pred: `enforce` does not fit CONTRACT (agency -> subject; enforcement actions only). Re-model it as a narrative/accusation edge: use `analytic`, or ask the contract owner for an accusation predicate. At minimum, flag the mismatch. 5) Remove c038 (Hindenburg) from this claim's contra list. It is not a denial of c020, has srcs=[], and the source never mentions Hindenburg. Keep c038 only as a gap note ("not asked / no statement located"). 6) Add to d: "Congress and Soros asked; did not immediately respond" (already present) plus the State Department spokesperson line, so the contra is complete. 7) The upgradeIf/killIf criteria are sound as written.

verdicts.dateTest: PASS. As a sentence: Rahul Gandhi (INC leader) demanded a JPC on the OCCRP Adani findings at a press conference in Mumbai on Thursday, 31 Aug 2023. The OCCRP follow-up is dated 1 Sep 2023 and says Gandhi spoke "at a press conference on Thursday", which was 31 Aug 2023. Onmanorama (31 Aug 2023) and Deccan Herald report the same Mumbai press conference. Gandhi's Lok Sabha membership had been restored on 7 Aug 2023, and he was a senior Congress leader but not Leader of the Opposition. The source never uses an office title, so no office is mis-dated. from=2023-08-31 is correct. to=null is acceptable, but no JPC was ever formed.
verdicts.identityTest: PASS on the entities. energy:inc = Indian National Congress, and OCCRP says "Indian National Congress leader Rahul Gandhi". grp:adani is a group node, which is institution-level framing, not a family. FAIL on the predicate. The CONTRACT defines `enforce` as "agency → subject: cancellation, suspension, freeze, investigation, sanction, debarment". Congress is a `ty: party`, not an agency. A demand for a JPC is not an enforcement action, and no JPC was ever constituted. In the graph this edge reads as "INC took enforcement action against Adani", which is false. Separately, the node id prefix `energy:` for a political party is an inherited cross-domain id. That is cosmetic, but worth noting.
verdicts.baseRate: Not discriminating. Opposition parties in India routinely demand JPCs on scandals that touch the government. Congress had already demanded a JPC on Adani after Hindenburg (Jan–Mar 2023) and repeated it through 2023–24. The BJP demanded JPCs itself when in opposition (2G, Bofors, coal allocation). In practice, almost every major corporate or political allegation (well over 80%) draws a JPC demand from the opposition of the day. So the demand says nothing about the merits of the OCCRP findings. Symmetry: the same rule, recording any party's press-conference demand as an `enforce` edge, would turn BJP JPC demands against Congress-era firms into "enforcement" too, which is absurd. The SPEC's holder and adviser controls do not apply to a political statement.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, and it was sought. OCCRP (1 Sep 2023): "On Thursday, the Adani Group reiterated the denials it had already issued to OCCRP reporters in response to the allegations" (https://www.occrp.org/en/news/indias-adani-group-faces-scrutiny-after-its-secret-investors-are-revealed). Adani's statement as reported by Onmanorama: "We categorically reject these recycled allegations. These news reports appear to be yet another concerted bid by Soros-funded interests supported by a section of the foreign media to revive the meritless Hindenburg report" (https://www.onmanorama.com/news/india/2023/08/31/ocrp-report-against-adani-group-rahul-gandhi-demands-jpc-probe.html). Later contrary development: on 3 Jan 2024 the Supreme Court (Vishal Tiwari v. Union of India) declined to transfer the probe to an SIT/CBI and called third-party reports such as OCCRP's unverified. The government never formed a JPC.
verdicts.innocentReading: The routine explanation fits: one day before an INDIA-bloc meeting, an opposition leader used a fresh foreign investigative report to attack the Prime Minister. That is ordinary opposition politics. The statement shows only that a demand was made. It is not evidence that "two foreigners manipulated the valuation". OCCRP alleged possible breach of promoter-holding and disclosure rules, not proven manipulation, so Gandhi's wording goes beyond his source.
verdicts.reason: The source confirms the fact. OCCRP quotes Gandhi word for word on 31 Aug 2023, and Onmanorama and Deccan Herald corroborate it, so the statement itself is documented. The edge still fails because of its encoding. `enforce` is reserved for an agency acting against a subject. A party's press-conference demand for a committee that was never constituted is not enforcement, so the graph would assert "INC enforced against Adani", which did not happen. No CONTRACT predicate covers "political demand". The content is already recorded in the energy:inc entity's `d` array and belongs in the narrative layer, so the edge should be removed rather than re-tiered. The tier also mixes two things. The statement is documented, but its substance ("manipulate the valuation") is an opposition allegation that the Supreme Court declined to act on in Jan 2024.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Remove c022 as a graph edge (pred `enforce` misapplied: `energy:inc` is ty=party, not an agency, and no enforcement action happened). Keep the content in energy:inc.d (already there) and in the relevant narrative (the OCCRP/Hindenburg narrative), with this wording: "Rahul Gandhi (INC) demanded a JPC at a Mumbai press conference, 31 Aug 2023 [documented statement; substance alleged]". 2) If the schema forces an edge anyway, keep tier `alleged` only for the substance. Add a second source (Onmanorama 31 Aug 2023, https://www.onmanorama.com/news/india/2023/08/31/ocrp-report-against-adani-group-rahul-gandhi-demands-jpc-probe.html). Add a note that no JPC was formed, and that the SC on 3 Jan 2024 (Vishal Tiwari v. UoI) declined an SIT/CBI transfer and treated the OCCRP material as unverified third-party reporting. That note should be a `supersede`/`contra` item. 3) Strengthen c023's contra text with Adani's actual words: "We categorically reject these recycled allegations ... Soros-funded interests ... revive the meritless Hindenburg report". This also ties the claim to the SPEC's "Soros funds a campaign" narrative. 4) Also relabel c023: its target `claim:narratives-literature:c022` should point to the OCCRP allegation claim, not to the political-demand claim, because Adani was denying OCCRP's findings, not responding to Gandhi. 5) Add a note that Gandhi's "manipulate the valuation" goes beyond OCCRP, which alleged possible breach of promoter-holding rules. 6) Cosmetic: the `energy:` prefix on the INC party node is an inherited cross-domain id. Consider a neutral id.

verdicts.dateTest: Restated: "[Project analysis, as of 2026-09-26] finds that the 'Rothschilds control central banks' trope has a documented propaganda lineage (1846 to the Nazi era) and has no Indian referent today." The timing checks out. RBI's About Us says: "Though originally privately owned, since nationalisation in 1949, the Reserve Bank is fully owned by the Government of India." That is current and covers the whole period since 1949. Rothschild & Co India Pvt Ltd was incorporated in 1998 (CIN U65990MH1998PTC116788) and is live on the firm's India page (2026-09). Dairnvaell's pamphlet (1846) and the Nazi films (1940) come before the analysis, as they should. One defect: the record has "from": "1999", which is the Ferguson paperback date. The analytic finding is a present-tense statement, so it should be dated to asOf 2026-09-26, not to when the book came out.
verdicts.identityTest: Mostly passes, with two defects. (1) t = cap:rothschild-co (Rothschild & Co SCA, Paris) is the right institutional referent. The Indian entity is identified correctly: the India page says it is "registered with the Securities and Exchange Board of India ('SEBI') as a Category-I Merchant Banker, bearing registration number INM000010668" and gives "Registered Number: U65990MH1998PTC116788", 1901 Altimus, Worli. The page also says "32 bankers based in India", but the record's d says "~30 bankers". (2) "Only an advisory subsidiary in India" / "the only Rothschild entity" is broader than what was checked. Edmond de Rothschild is a separate Swiss group outside the Rothschild & Co perimeter, and neither this file nor the sibling holders files examined it (AUDIT.json already flags this gap). The wording has to be narrowed to Rothschild & Co. (3) s = cap:lit-ferguson-house-of-rothschild is a book, not an actor. SPEC says outright that historical Rothschild banking (Ferguson) is "context for the narrative ladder ..., not a node". A graph edge from a family history book to a present-day firm visually ties the modern company to the trope. This content already exists, correctly placed, in the narratives entry ("The Rothschilds control the RBI / Indian banking").
verdicts.baseRate: This claim is a debunk, not an attribution, so a discriminating base rate matters less here. The absence finding is not specific to Rothschild. Among foreign advisers in the SPEC control set (Lazard, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, JP Morgan, Citi), 0 of 6 or more hold an RBI board seat or an Indian banking-licence stake through their advisory arms. The RBI is 100% GoI-owned for every one of them. The "no Indian referent" result would come out the same for Lazard, and that is the correct reading: it describes the Indian central bank's ownership, not anything about Rothschild. The symmetry holds.
verdicts.denialFound: None found. Not asked, and no response is needed: the claim accuses Rothschild & Co of nothing. The firm's own India page (https://www.rothschildandco.com/en/countries/india/) describes itself as providing "M&A and Strategic Advisory, Global Markets Solutions including fundraising and strategic capital..." and mentions no banking licence. That is a self-description, not a denial.
verdicts.innocentReading: The boring explanation fits completely. A 200-year-old banking name, with a real 1820s–1870s peak that Ferguson documents, keeps a shorthand alive. The firm's marketing ("25+ years of experience in India", "145 M&A deals since 2010") suggests more scale than its licence category (a SEBI Cat-I merchant banker, with no bank, lending or deposit-taking) supports. Meanwhile the RBI is state-owned by statute.
verdicts.reason:
The core analytic conclusion survives, because every part of it rests on a primary or encyclopaedic source I opened. (a) RBI About Us: "since nationalisation in 1949, the Reserve Bank is fully owned by the Government of India." (b) The Rothschild & Co India page: SEBI Cat-I merchant banker INM000010668, advisory services only. (c) Wikipedia, Rothschild family: "These theories take differing forms, such as claiming that the family controls the world's wealth and financial institutions" and "Most conspiracy theories about the Rothschild family arise from antisemitic prejudice and various antisemitic tropes." The same page names the Nazi propaganda films Der ewige Jude and Die Rothschilds, and says "The family's wealth declined over the 20th century and was divided among many descendants." Analytic is the right tier, and the record carries an innocentReading.

The source chain in `d` has a real defect, though. The cited "Rothschild family" page (live wikitext, 2026-09) never mentions Dairnvaell or 1846, and never calls the Waterloo story fictional. That passage is on the Nathan Mayer Rothschild page: "The Rothschild family and others have claimed that this embellished version of events originated in Mathieu-Dairnvaell's 1846 writing, was further embellished by John Reeves in 1887...". It is also framed there as a claim attributed to others, citing Ferguson, not as "fictional". The Penguin Random House page is a publisher's blurb and says nothing about the trope. If anything its line about "the family's vast political network, which gave it access to and influence over many of the greatest statesmen of the age" belongs in the strongestCase. So the source check is only partial, and the fixes below are needed. None of them overturns the finding.
verdicts.corrections:
1. In d, replace "the encyclopaedic summary, citing Ferguson, traces the control myth to the fictional Waterloo legend, Dairnvaell's 1846 pamphlet and Nazi propaganda" with: "Wikipedia (Rothschild family) says most Rothschild conspiracy theories 'arise from antisemitic prejudice and various antisemitic tropes' and records Nazi propaganda films (Der ewige Jude, Die Rothschilds). Wikipedia (Nathan Mayer Rothschild), citing Ferguson, records that the embellished Waterloo-speculation story is said to originate in Mathieu-Dairnvaell's 1846 pamphlet and was re-embellished by Reeves (1887)." Add the source ["Wikipedia — Nathan Mayer Rothschild", "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathan_Mayer_Rothschild"]. Do not use the word "fictional"; the source says "embellished".
2. Relabel the Penguin Random House source as bibliographic only (it establishes the book's existence, 1 Nov 1999, ISBN 9780140240849). It does not support the trope-lineage statement. The AHR abstract is the scholarly-reception source.
3. Narrow the wording from "only an advisory subsidiary in India" / "the only Rothschild entity" to "Rothschild & Co's only Indian entity is one SEBI Cat-I merchant-banking/advisory subsidiary". Add to gaps: "Edmond de Rothschild (a separate Swiss group) not checked."
4. Change "~30 bankers" to "32 bankers based in India (firm's India page, 2026-09)".
5. Change "from": "1999" to "2026-09-26" (the date of the analysis), or null.
6. Structure: SPEC says Ferguson/historical Rothschild banking is "context ..., not a node". Prefer removing the edge cap:lit-ferguson-house-of-rothschild → cap:rothschild-co and keeping this content only in the narratives entry and the voids entry, with Ferguson as a source rather than a node. If the edge is kept, it must stay pred/tier analytic, and the RBI and Rothschild & Co India URLs must stay in srcs. The task-level srcs list gives only PRH and Wikipedia, and neither supports the "RBI 100% GoI-owned" or "advisory subsidiary" halves.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim restated: the Governments of India (Ministry of Finance/CBDT) and Mauritius signed a Protocol to the 1982 DTAA on 10 May 2016. Under it, India gets the right to tax capital gains on Indian-company shares acquired on or after 1 Apr 2017, and shares acquired before then are grandfathered. Separately, Mauritius was the conduit for more than a third of FDI in 2000–15. The dates are consistent: the protocol was signed in May 2016 and the new rule took effect on 1 Apr 2017. The FDI window (2000–15) comes before the change, which fits a claim that this was the basis of the narrative. The date fields are wrong, though. "to":"2017-04-01" treats the effective date as an end date. The rule did not end in 2017; it took effect then and is still in force. The 2024 protocol adds a principal-purpose test but does not replace the capital-gains rule in Art. 13(3A)/(3B).
verdicts.identityTest: The treaty is identified correctly: the India–Mauritius DTAA of 1982, amended by the Protocol of 10 May 2016. The Indian treaty party is the Union Government, where the Ministry of Finance/CBDT is the competent authority, so the node min:ministry-of-finance is acceptable. However, the entities actually governed by the rule are Mauritius-resident investors in Indian shares, not the Ministry of Finance. The KSL article (Gunputh, Jha & Pudaruth, KSLR 5(2) 29–41, published 30 Nov 2017) is the one the claim cites.
verdicts.baseRate: This claim describes a legal rule, not a property that singles out one entity. Mauritius's share of cumulative FDI equity (about 33–34% for Apr 2000–Mar 2015, per DIPP factsheets) makes it the single largest source, so the property is discriminating. The symmetry check points the same way. Singapore's DTAA carried the same capital-gains exemption, was amended in the same direction by a protocol in Dec 2016, and Singapore is the second-largest FDI conduit. Cyprus's treaty was also revised in 2016. So "treaty-shopping jurisdiction" is not unique to Mauritius. Anyone reading "Mauritius = round-tripping" should be told that the Singapore route received identical treatment.
verdicts.denialFound: No denial found from the party concerned, and none is needed: the Union Government itself made this change. From memory rather than an opened source, the CBDT/PIB press release of 10 May 2016 framed the protocol as tackling "treaty abuse and round tripping of funds attributed to the India-Mauritius treaty". That is an admission by the governing party, not a denial, and it should be opened and cited. Mauritius (its government and FSC) has repeatedly rejected being described as a round-tripping haven. The KSL abstract notes the "win-win" ties and that Mauritius is only "considered a tax haven". No specific rejoinder was pulled for this claim, and Mauritius was not asked.
verdicts.innocentReading: Before 2017, most FDI routed through Mauritius was lawful treaty use by genuine foreign investors (PE funds, MNC holding companies). The Supreme Court upheld this in Union of India v Azadi Bachao Andolan (2003), relying on CBDT Circular 789 on tax residency certificates. A large share of FDI arriving via Mauritius therefore shows treaty shopping for the tax exemption. On its own it does not show that Indian black money was round-tripped. The claim's parenthetical describes the narrative correctly and does not assert that round-tripping happened. It should be kept that way.
verdicts.reason: Both sources confirm what the claim says. NTU CAS (29 Apr 2024): "The revision granted India the right to tax capital gains on sales of shares in Indian companies, effective from 1 April 2017." "Investments made before this date are exempted from such taxation." "Between 2000 to 2015, over a third of all foreign investments into India were channelled through Mauritius." "...roundtripping their investments back into India via shell entities based in Mauritius." The KSL abstract says: "Mauritius contributes to nearly 34% of total Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) flow into India" and describes India amending the DTAA "to prevent round tripping and consequently treaty shopping." Practitioner alerts (Pillsbury, KPMG, Kluwer, Cyril Amarchand) independently confirm the mechanics: Art. 13(3A) applies to shares acquired after 1 Apr 2017, with grandfathering; Art. 13(3B) sets the rate at 50% of the domestic rate until 31 Mar 2019, subject to LoB. Nothing refutes the claim. "Reported" is the right tier for now because the primary protocol text and the CBDT/PIB release were not opened. Opening either would support "documented".
verdicts.corrections: 1) The text says "source-based capital-gains tax from 1 Apr 2017". Change it to "India may tax gains on Indian-company shares acquired on/after 1 Apr 2017; shares acquired earlier grandfathered". The rule turns on the acquisition date, not the date the gain is realised. 2) Set "from":"2016-05-10" (signing date) and record 2017-04-01 in d as the effective date. Set "to": null; the rule is still in force. 3) Remove supersededBy "narratives-literature:c030". The 2024 PPT protocol adds to the capital-gains rule but does not replace it. If a link is wanted, use a relation rather than supersession. 4) Update d: the 50% transitional rate (for shares acquired from 1 Apr 2017 and sold by 31 Mar 2019) and the LoB test are now confirmed by https://www.pillsburylaw.com/en/news-and-insights/four-things-you-need-to-know-about-the-mauritius-india-protocol-1.html and https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmg/pdf/2016/05/taxalert-201616.pdf. 5) In d, record that the KSL figure is "nearly 34%" and the NTU figure is "over a third". 6) Add upgradeIf: open the CBDT/PIB press release of 10 May 2016 or the protocol on incometaxindia.gov.in, then set the tier to documented. 7) Add a symmetry note: the Singapore DTAA was amended the same way in Dec 2016 (Singapore is the other major conduit). 8) Add innocentReading: the Azadi Bachao Andolan (2003) ruling upheld treaty use, and conduit share is not evidence of round-tripping. 9) Consider changing the target from min:ministry-of-finance to the investors it governs (Mauritius-resident FPI/FDI vehicles). Under the law predicate, the direction is rule to governed.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim form: <no official body (SIT, SEBI, CBDT, courts)> <published> <a share of ODI or FPI assets that is Indian-resident round-tripped money> <from 2014, when ODIs were defined in the FPI Regulations, to Sep 2026>. Every dated anchor falls inside the window: SIT third report Jul 2015 (ODIs Rs 2.715 lakh crore, Feb 2015), treaty protocols of 2016 and Mar 2024, SEBI rules of 2016, 2017 and Aug 2023, and the SEBI board memo of Sep 2025 on resident-Indian contributions to FPIs (opened, no aggregate figure). Nothing collapses. One caveat: the Arthapedia sentence "this has not been proved so far" is undated and predates the 2016 and 2017 reforms, so it cannot cover the period after 2023. The claim's "from 2014" also sits awkwardly with the word "ever".
verdicts.identityTest: These are institutional nodes, so the person-identity rules do not apply. cap:p-notes-odi matches what Arthapedia names: "Offshore Derivative Instrument (ODIs) in Section 2(1)(j)" of the SEBI FPI Regulations, Jan 2014. cap:india-mauritius-dtaa matches NTU CAS: the 1982 DTAA, amended in 2016 and by the Mar 2024 protocol (PPT). The edge from p-notes-odi to india-mauritius-dtaa is loose. The only documented tie is SEBI's figure, carried by the SIT, that Mauritius held 9.91% of ODI beneficial-owner locations. NTU's "over a third" figure is about FDI, not ODIs or FPI assets.
verdicts.baseRate: The absence does not single out Mauritius. No Indian official source publishes an Indian-resident round-tripped share for any conduit (Cayman 31.31%, USA 14.20%, UK 13.49%, Mauritius 9.91%, Bermuda 9.10% of ODI beneficial-owner locations in Feb 2015). It is also missing for Singapore and the Netherlands on the FDI side. Few regulators anywhere publish a look-through residency numerator, so the void is close to 100% across comparable jurisdictions. That is why it counts as a finding about the record and not as evidence either way. The only quantified round-tripping estimate I found is academic and covers FDI, not FPI or ODIs: Rao & Dhar (ISID/RIS 2011) put about 19.5% of FDI in Sep 2004 to Dec 2009 as "prone to round-tripping" (India-related investors 10.3%, India-related PE 4.0%, NRIs 5.2%).
verdicts.denialFound: No accused party. This is an absence claim, and the party concerned is the state's own record. The nearest official position is the Indian Economic Service's Arthapedia (ies.gov.in/arthapedia/concept/participatory-notes-pns): "There are also concerns that some of the money coming into the market via PNs could be the unaccounted wealth camouflaged under the guise of FII investment. However, this has not been proved so far." SEBI's Sep 2025 board memo (sebi.gov.in/sebi_data/meetingfiles/sep-2025/1758513369924_1.pdf) sets out the rules for resident Indians as FPI constituents (below 25% each and below 50% in aggregate with NRIs/OCIs, up to 100% for some IFSC FPIs) but gives no aggregate share. No official source contradicting the claim was found. SEBI, CBDT and MoF were not asked.
verdicts.innocentReading: Nobody published a numerator because the regime was built to make it structurally zero or to route it through legal channels. Residents and NRIs are barred from subscribing to ODIs. Their participation in FPIs is capped and goes through LRS/ODI rules. SEBI's 2016, 2017 and 2023 regimes collect beneficial-owner data for supervision, not publication. The large Mauritius share is also explained by non-residents doing tax arbitrage, so its size says nothing about who the ultimate owners are. The absence may therefore reflect a regulatory design choice rather than concealment. It cuts both ways: it neither confirms nor kills the narrative.
verdicts.reason: This could not be refuted as a scoped absence finding. The two cited sources support the structural half: NTU CAS says "Between 2000 to 2015, over a third of all foreign investments into India were channelled through Mauritius". Arthapedia carries the SIT/SEBI figure of Rs 2.715 lakh crore in ODIs with beneficial-owner locations, and says the unaccounted-wealth concern "has not been proved so far". The absence half is backed by my own searches of SEBI, SIT and MoF material: no official figure for the Indian-resident share of ODI or FPI assets turned up. The only quantified estimate is academic (Rao & Dhar) and covers FDI. The problem is the wording in the text I was given: "No official record ever quantified" is a universal negative that the evidence cannot carry. The file's own lab and d are correctly scoped to "any official record opened" and "opened this session". The sources confirm the structure but cannot confirm the negative, hence sourceCheck is partially. Analytic is the right tier because this is our inference from a documented void. It carries innocentReading, upgradeIf and killIf, and implies no wrongdoing by anyone.
verdicts.corrections: 1. Replace the text "No official record ever quantified…" with the file's scoped form: "No official record opened (SIT 2015, SEBI 2016/2017/2023/2025 papers, treaty protocols) quantifies the share of ODI/FPI assets that is Indian-resident round-tripped money; structure documented, numerator absent." Remove "ever". 2. Add to d that SEBI did quantify ODI beneficial-owner jurisdictions (via SIT, Feb 2015: Cayman 31.31%, USA 14.20%, UK 13.49%, Mauritius 9.91%, Bermuda 9.10%) and that India is absent because residents and NRIs are barred from ODIs. That is the closest official numerator, and the reader should see it. 3. Note that NTU's "over a third" and the 2000–15 Mauritius share refer to FDI, not ODI or FPI assets. Add Rao & Dhar 2011 (ISID/RIS, mpra.ub.uni-muenchen.de/29153) as the only quantified estimate, about 19.5% of FDI prone to round-tripping, labelled academic and FDI so it is not read as an official FPI numerator. 4. Add the Arthapedia quote "However, this has not been proved so far" as the state-side statement, with the caveat that it is undated and predates the 2016 reforms. 5. Add SEBI's Sep 2025 board memo (sebi.gov.in/sebi_data/meetingfiles/sep-2025/1758513369924_1.pdf) as an opened official record that sets resident-Indian FPI contribution limits but publishes no aggregate. 6. Record that SEBI, CBDT and MoF were not asked. 7. Consider retargeting or annotating the edge: the p-notes-odi to india-mauritius-dtaa link rests only on Mauritius's 9.91% share of ODI beneficial-owner locations.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim as a sentence: "SEBI gave Jio BlackRock final MF registration 7.7 months after in-principle (4 Oct 2024 to 26/27 May 2025), against about 19 months for Bajaj and longer for other comparators." Jio's dates come from mandates-ventures c030–c032, not from this claim's srcs. The durations hold: 351 days to in-principle and 234–235 days to final. The AUDIT found that "26 May" is not in the BS source, which says the company announced it on Tuesday, 27 May 2025. Bajaj's final leg runs from 23 Aug 2021 to the announcement on about 1 Mar 2023, which is about 18 months, not "~19" (AUDIT.json, c039 review). Old Bridge: Business Today, publication dated 6 Sep 2023, says "has received the final approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to commence its mutual fund operations". It gives no approval date, no in-principle date and no application date, so 2023-09-06 is the publication date, not the grant date. Angel One: The Week/PTI says "Sebi has granted a certificate of registration to Angel One Mutual Fund on November 25, 2024". It gives no in-principle date. Neither opened source supplies the in-principle date that a final-leg comparison needs.
verdicts.identityTest: The entities match. Angel One Asset Management Company Ltd (wholly-owned subsidiary of Angel One Ltd) is the AMC for Angel One Mutual Fund, per PTI, and it matches t = cap:angel-one-amc. Old Bridge Capital Management / Old Bridge Mutual Fund matches the control node. Jio BlackRock Asset Management is the AMC registered 2025. There is a node mismatch: the claim's decisive comparator is Bajaj (~19 months), but t is Angel One, whose final leg is not established by any opened source. The edge therefore links s to a node whose relevant datum (the in-principle date) the record says was not opened. No family, religion or ethnicity is framed as the actor.
verdicts.baseRate: The claim's comparative clause, "longer for comparators whose in-principle dates were not opened", is asserted without evidence, and the record's d-field goes further: "faster than every comparator whose dates are known". A same-period comparator contradicts this. Capitalmind got in-principle approval 26 Aug 2024 (BS, search result) and final approval announced 14 Apr 2025. Capitalmind's own release says "just over seven months after the in-principle approval" (https://www.capitalmind.in/insights/welcoming-the-capitalmind-mutual-fund, opened). That is about 7.5 months against Jio BlackRock's 7.7. Among 2024–25 entrants whose dates are known, a final leg of about 7–8 months is ordinary, not exceptional. This comes close to the record's own killIf ("6–9-month final legs as the norm"), although it rests on one datapoint, not a SEBI series. Bajaj (2021–23, through COVID) and the pre-2023 cohort (Angel One in-principle 8 Feb 2023 per snippet, Zerodha Sep 2021, Helios) come from a slower backlog era, so comparing across eras inflates Jio's apparent speed. Others not opened: Unifi in-principle Nov 2023 (BS 20 Nov 2023, not opened); Choice AMC final 1 Aug 2025 (in-principle date not found).
verdicts.denialFound: None found. Not asked. No accusation is made against SEBI or JFS/BlackRock that they would need to answer, and SEBI publishes no processing-time statistics. Jio Financial/Jio BlackRock's releases (BS 27 May 2025) state the dates without comment on timing.
verdicts.innocentReading: The final leg (in-principle to registration) is mostly applicant-controlled set-up work: incorporating the AMC and trustee, capital infusion, hiring, systems. After SEBI cleared its 2023 backlog, well-capitalised 2024 in-principle holders cleared it in about 7 months as a matter of course. Capitalmind, a small Bengaluru PMS firm with no political connection, took "just over seven months" in the same window. The sponsor-fitness leg (in-principle) took Jio 11.5 months, no faster than Bajaj's 11. BlackRock's prior Indian AMC experience and its systems further shorten set-up.
verdicts.reason: Both opened sources confirm only final-approval facts. Old Bridge's source does not even give the grant date, only the publication date. Neither source supports the claim's comparative clause that the final leg was "longer for comparators whose in-principle dates were not opened". The record admits that clause rests on unopened search snippets. A reachable same-period comparator (Capitalmind: in-principle 26 Aug 2024, final Apr 2025, "just over seven months" per its own release) contradicts the record's assertion that Jio BlackRock "was faster than every comparator whose dates are known" on the final leg. Bajaj's ~19 months is also ~18 per the AUDIT. The analytic conclusion (no evidence of fast-tracking; the in-principle leg was not faster) survives and is strengthened, but the comparative text as written is refuted and must be rewritten before publication.
